segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᏅ ᏝᎦ ᏙᏓᏛᏢᏃᎮᏟ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ. ᏄᏍᏓᏭᏅ ᎤᏃᏪᎳ ᏛᎬᏯᏛᏛᎮᏢᏂ. ᏃᎴ Ꮕ ᏍᎫ ᎯᎢ ᏥᏓᏅᏕᎵᏆ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏯᎾᏕᏠᎩ ᎠᏯ ᎢᎩᏬᏂᏒ ᏥᏓᏂᏂᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏢᏴ ᎡᎵᏫ ᏍᎫ ᏢᏴ ᏰᏨᏌ ᏧᏂᏂᏛᏅ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏴᎲᏛᎦᎦ ᎢᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏴᎾᏛᎦᎦ Ꭰ ᏥᏓᏂᏂᏗᎭ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏙᏕᏣᏙ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎬᏗ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ Ꮕ
segments.transliteration: hinv tlaga dodadvtlvnohetli atsalagiha. nusdawunv unowela dvgvyadvdvhetlvni. nole nv sgu hii tsidanvdeliqua diniyotli eliwu gusda yanadetlogi aya igiwonisv tsidaninidi nole sgu tlvyv eliwi sgu tlvyv yetsvsa tsuninidvnv hiwonisgv yvhvdvgaga iniwonisgv yvnadvgaga a tsidaninidiha aseno dodetsado yonega gvdi atsalagi nv
segments.translation: Now, we’re going to talk for a little bit in Cherokee, and I’m going to ask you what they have written. And maybe the students will learn something from this recording. Maybe at some point they will give you this recording and you can hear yourself talking, and us talking. What’s your name in English and what’s your name in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: Harry Daugherty, ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ
segments.transliteration: Harry Daugherty, aniyosgi
segments.translation: Harry Daugherty. Soldiers.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ
segments.transliteration: aniyosgi
segments.translation: Soldiers

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎲᏍᎩᏂ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ last name Daugherty. Ꮂ ᎥᎬᏛᎦᏅ ᏱᎦ
segments.transliteration: hvsgini yawanvti tsalagi gvdi last name Daugherty. hv vgvdvganv yiga
segments.translation: I don’t know my last name in Cherokee. Daugherty. I've never heard it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᏘᏴ Commod ᏗᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏁᎵᏍᎪᎯ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏌᏗᏒ ᏫᎾ ᏗᏢ ᏬᏤᏙ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᎾᎥ ᏬᏥᏯᏙᎲ *truck*Ꭲ ᏤᎲ ᎩᎶ *Rider* ᏧᏙᎢᏓ *Daugherty* ᎯᏲᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: etiyv Commod digilvwisdane tsigehv nelisgohi tsudetiyvsadisv wina ditlv wotsedo tsigesv tsuyohusv nav wotsiyadohv *truck*i tsehv gilo *Rider* tsudoida *Daugherty* hiyolige tsigehe?
segments.translation: A long time ago, when I used to work with food distribution back in the ‘80s, we used to go out by Belfonte, giving out food in a truck. There used to be a person living there named Rider Daugherty. Did you know him?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎠᎮᎾ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏛᏂ ᏱᎨᎮᎢ. ᏍᎨᏲ ᏱᎾᏂᏫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃᏲ ᎡᏚᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏱᎦᏪᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎩᎶ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏗᎾᏓᏛᏂ ᎢᏦᏎᎮᏍᏗ. ᎮᏍᏗ ᎯᏛᏱᎸᎢ ᏍᎫᏭ ᏄᏍᏕᏍᏗ ᎠᏬᏎ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᎩᎶ ᏥᏓᏱᎸ ᏱᎩ ᏗᎾᏓᏛᏂ ᏯᏬᏎᎵ ᏣᎾᏛᏂ ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: vv ahena tla gohusdi tsosdadadvni yigehei. sgeyo yinaniwi tsigehv asenoyo edudi tsigehv yigawesgi tsigehv gilo gohusdi dinadadvni itsosehesdi. hesdi hidvyilvi sguwu nusdesdi awose tsigehv tla alvhiyu gilo tsidayilv yigi dinadadvni yawoseli tsanadvni nusdidanv gelisgo
segments.translation: Yeah, but we weren’t related. That’s what they used to say, but my grandpa used to say that if someone tells you we’re related, don’t deny it. Just leave it like that. I never denied anyone who said we were related. I would just think “I guess you know what you’re talking about.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯᎮ ᏍᏊ ᎾᎩᏪᏎᎸ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏗᏟ ᎤᏕᎵᎬ ᏗᏟ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏥᏚᎾᏙᎥ ᎣᏂ ᏗᏟ ᏥᏓᏩᏙ ᏥᏥᏯᏛᏛᏅ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎩᏗ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏪᏒ ᎪᎱᏍᏛ ᎢᏓᏓᏛᏂ ᎠᏅᏗᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᏕᎭᏛᏂᎸᎨᏍᏚᏭ ᎬᏬᏎᎸ ᎨᏒ
segments.transliteration: ayahe squu nagiweselv tsigehv elisi tsigehv vna ditli udeligv ditli utloyi tsidunadov oni ditli tsidawado tsitsiyadvdvnv saquu yuwagidi squu sgi tsinuwesv gohusdv idadadvni anvdisgesdi dehadvnilvgesduwu gvwoselv gesv
segments.translation: That’s what my grandma used to say, because there were some people in the east with the same last name as us. I asked her about it, and she said the same thing, “If they say they’re related to us, just show them respect.”

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎠᏩᏛᎯᏍᏛᏅ ᎠᏯ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ ᎠᏮᏛ ᎯᏍᏗᏗᏒ ᎠᏫᏴ ᏥᏂᎦᏛ ᎡᏠᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᏴᏅᎲ ᎡᏥᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᏲᎱᏎᎸ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎮᏂ ᎯᏍᎩ ᏃᏥᎥ ᎣᏨᏢᏅᏢ ᎾᏂ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎣᎩᏲᎱᏎᎸ ᎤᏕᏘᏴᏚᏭ Ꮲ ᎡᏥ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᎯᎢᏃ ᏞᏍᏗ ᎰᏩ ᏱᏥᏯᏅᏛᏗ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎩᏍᏗᎩ ᏛᎮ ᎨᎮ ᎡᏠᎩ ᎠᎩᏴᏅᎲ *Greasy* ᏓᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᎪᎯᏗ, ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏛᎮ Ꮲ. ᏃᎴ *Texas* ᏄᎾᏛᏂᏛᏅ ᏃᎴ ᎢᎬᎩᏘᏅᏒ ᏍᏊ ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏚ Ꮲ ᎥᎾ ᏧᏩᏪᏙᎸ ᏃᎴ ᏨᎩᎷᏨ. ᎡᏚᏥ ᏤᏙᎲ *California* ᎡᎯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᎩᏴᏅᎲ ᎬᏮᎸᏨ ᏅᏮᏁᎸ ᏛᏩᎸᏘᏍᏗ *California* ᏮᎩᏘᏃᏢ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎠᏫᏴ ᏥᏂᎦᏛ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏖ ᏗᏢ ᏩᎩᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᎯᏍᎩ ᏑᏓᎵ ᎴᏱᎩ ᏱᏧᏕᏘᏴᏗ ᏩᏩᏕᏅ ᎥᎾ ᏁᎳᏚ ᎾᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏓᏩᏂᎩᏒ
segments.transliteration: ayadv sgi nusda awadvhisdvnv aya sgi hena anigayvli awvdv hisdidisv awiyv tsinigadv etlogi heni agiyvnvhv etsiheni agiyohuselv agisdi tsigehv aheni hisgi notsiv otsvtlvnvtlv nani usdi ogiyohuselv udetiyvduwu tlv etsi tsuyohusv hiino tlesdi howa yitsiyanvdvdi etsi tsigehv vgisdigi dvhe gehe etlogi agiyvnvhv *Greasy* dawadeloquav gohidi, sudetiyvdvhe tlv. nole *Texas* nunadvnidvnv nole igvgitinvsv squu sudetiyvdu tlv vna tsuwawedolv nole tsvgilutsv. edutsi tsedohv *California* ehi sgina tsagiyvnvhv gvwvlvtsv nvwvnelv dvwalvtisdi *California* wvgitinotlv aseno awiyv tsinigadv tla yawanate ditlv wagilohisdi hisgi sudali leyigi yitsudetiyvdi wawadenv vna neladu nawadetiyvda dawanigisv
segments.translation: That’s how I was raised. The elders raised me. When I was this tall [gestures] my aunt took me in, because when I was little, I lost my mom. There was five of us, but we lost the youngest one when they were a year old. When we lost our mom I don’t remember that well because I was little. My aunt went to Greasy for a while, probably about a year. Then they went to Texas, and they took me. I went there for about a year and came back. My uncle from California was here and he took me in and took me to California, and I couldn’t escape from California. I was just ye tall [gestures] and I didn’t know which way to go. I was there for about five or six years, and I came back when I was 18 years old.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏗᏣᏂᎩᏎ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, ditsanigise
segments.translation: Yeah, you left from there.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏃᏭ ᏂᎬ ᏍᎩ ᎾᎩᏍᏗᏕᎩ ᏥᎦᏴᎳᎩ ᏍᎩ ᎾᏩᏛᏅᏕᎬ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎬᏲᏎᎲ *Construction* ᏥᏩᏩᏖᎸᏛ ᏃᏭᏂ *United States* ᏂᎬ ᏥᎨᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv nowu nigv sgi nagisdidegi tsigayvlagi sgi nawadvnvdegv sgi heni tsigvyosehv *Construction* tsiwawatelvdv nowuni *United States* nigv tsigedohv
segments.translation: I just kind of went everywhere and I’ve gotten old like that. I was in construction and went all over the United States.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎣᎣ ᏙᎲ ᏂᎬ ᏤᏙᎵᏙᎸ?
segments.transliteration: oo dohv nigv tsedolidolv?
segments.translation: Oh, you’ve been all over the place.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏙᏅ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ Sam ᎢᎮᏂ ᏚᏙ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ. Ꮎ ᎬᏅᎯᏙ ᎾᎥ ᎡᎯ. “Truck ᏗᎯᎵᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᏛᏲ ᎤᎪᏗ ᎠᏪᏙᎸ” ᏧᏛᏅ “Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏱᎨᎵ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎭᏢᏍᏗᎰᏭᏲ ᎠᏱᏲ ᎨᏙᎰ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ
segments.transliteration: donv tsosdadanvtli Sam iheni dudo tsosdadanvtli. na gvnvhido nav ehi. “Truck dihilido tsigehv aya dvyo ugodi awedolv” tsudvnv “tla gohusdi yigeli” tsiyohelv “hatlvsdihowuyo ayiyo gedoho” tsiyohelv
segments.translation: My brother’s name is Sam Daugherty. He lives over there in Long. “I drive a truck and I’ve been to more places than you,” he told me. I said, “I don’t care you just drive by and I’ve actually been to places.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏭᏂᏴ ᎭᏢᏍᏗᎰ ᎬᎪᏘᎰ ᎯᏲᎮᎴ
segments.transliteration: awuniyv hatlvsdiho gvgotiho hiyohele
segments.translation: So, you told him you just drive on by.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏥᏂᏥᏪᏎᎸ ᏅᎨ ᏗᏢ Ꮎ ᎥᎩᏙ 51 ᏪᎦᏅᏅ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᏄᎲ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᎩᏲᎱᏎᎸ ᎤᏩᏏᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎠᎩᎧᎲ. ᎠᏫᏴ ᎠᎩᏢᏍᏗᎰ ᏱᏫᎤᎷᏨ ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᏧᏅᏢᏃᎮᏗ ᏗᎬᏗᏍᎪ “Ꮩ ᎤᏛᏅᏕᎩ ᎩᏂᏙᎠ?” ᎯᏑᎳᎪᎢ Sam ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎰ ᎠᏭᏂ ᏣᎵᏢᏍᏗ ᎪᎯ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏯᎴᏫᏍᏗ ᏥᏲᎮᎰ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᎴᏫᏍᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: sgidv tsinitsiweselv nvge ditlv na vgido 51 weganvnv tsuyohusv hilvsgi nuhv tsigesv agiyohuselv uwasinv squu vgido agikahv. awiyv agitlvsdiho yiwiulutsv tsuwenvhv tsunvtlvnohedi digvdisgo “do udvnvdegi ginidoa?” hisulagoi Sam tsitsiyoheho awuni tsalitlvsdi gohi tla squu yalewisdi tsiyoheho tsulenvhv alewisdihv
segments.translation: That’s what I told my sister who lives on 51. She passed away not too long ago, and she was my only sister. He just drives by and gets home and calls me and asked me how our sister is doing. And I say, “Shut up, Sam! You just drove by and you should’ve stopped.” He started stopping by after that.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏅ ᏥᎵᏃᎮᏛᏅ sam ᏧᎶᏒ ᏙᎭ
segments.transliteration: sginv tsilinohedvnv sam tsulosv doha
segments.translation: You talk to Sam too huh? He came through.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎤᏃᎮᏞ ᏥᏯᏐᎮᎸ
segments.transliteration: unohetle tsiyasohelv
segments.translation: Did he tell you all I got on to him?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: huh-uh
segments.transliteration: huh-uh
segments.translation: huh-uh

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᏕᏞᏛᎮ
segments.transliteration: udetledvhe
segments.translation: He kept it to himself.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎠᏪᏛᏴ ᏴᏛᏢᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏯᏙᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᎦ ᎨᎲ ᏳᏫᎤᎷᏨ ᏃᏭᏛ ᏧᎾᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᏭᎵᏍᏕᏲ ᎠᎦᏴᎵ ᏗᎧᏂᏗ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ ᏫᎩ ᎣᎩᏅᏏ ᎮᎾ ᏃᏭ ᎣᏍᏕ.
segments.transliteration: awedvyv yvdvtlvsdi gehv yadohisdi yiga gehv yuwiulutsv nowudv tsunatlanohedi wulisdeyo agayvli dikanidi usdikani wigi oginvsi hena nowu osde.
segments.translation: He’d drive right on by, honk his horn, get all the way home and call me. Boy, he looks old. He’s the youngest too. It’s just him and I.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᏛᏏᏭᎮ
segments.transliteration: sdvsiwuhe
segments.translation: So just you two now.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎾᎮ ᎤᏔᏂᏗ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ ᏤᎲ Nicut. John ᏥᏚᏙᎥ, John Daugherty. ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏧᏪᏥ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᏍᎩ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᏣᎩᎧᏂᎦ ᎪᎯ. ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎬᏩᎦᏎᏍᏗᏕᎦ. Ꮭ ᎠᏎ ᏍᎩᎦᏎᏍᏙᏗ ᏱᎩ Ꮟ ᏕᎦᏤᏟ ᏂᎯ ᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎨᎲ. ᏳᏓᎭ ᏛᏎ ᎬᎩᏁᎵᏍᎪ ᏓᏩᏟᏴᏒ. ᎠᎮᏂ ᎠᏯᏛ Ꮭ ᎡᏠᏪ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᎮᏂ ᏙᏛᎬᏟᏴ.
segments.transliteration: nahe utanidi tsosdadanvtli tsehv Nicut. John tsidudov, John Daugherty. sgiheni tsuwetsi anitsutsa sgi usdayvhvsgi tsagikaniga gohi. sgiheni gvwagasesdidega. tla ase sgigasesdodi yigi si degatsetli nihi tsiyohehv gehv. yudaha dvse gvginelisgo dawatliyvsv. aheni ayadv tla etlowe yigehe aheni dodvgvtliyv.
segments.translation: My oldest brother lived in Nicut. His name was John Daugherty. His wife’s sons brought me over. They’ve been watching me. I told them they don’t have to watch me. “I’m doing better than y’all,” I told them. Sometimes I think they get mad at me for saying the things I do, but I fight back at them because I’m not going to be quiet about it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎭᏢᎩ ᏣᏕᎾ ᎨᏒ ᏃᎴ ᎯᎳᏴ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏌᏗᏎ ᏣᏕᏂᏞ
segments.transliteration: hatlvgi tsadena gesv nole hilayv tsudetiyvsadise tsadenitle
segments.translation: Where were you born and what year were you born?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎠᏫ ᏥᎨ ....... five years ᏛᎮ ᏃᏭ ᏂᎨᎣ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏥᏁᎵ
segments.transliteration: awi tsige ....... five years dvhe nowu nigeo una tsitsineli
segments.translation: Where I live now, I’ve been there for five years.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎲ yeah
segments.transliteration: vhv yeah
segments.translation: Yeah

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏃᎮᏂ SalemᎢ ᎾᎥ ᏥᏁᎵ ᎡᏍᏗᏟᏴ CC campᎢ ᎤᏟᏗᏟ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏁᎵ ᎯᏍᎩ ᏛᏃ ᎾᏕᏘᏴ ᎤᎾ ᎬᎩᎷᏨ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎾᎮᏂ ᏭᎨᏗᎵᏴ ᏥᎨᎥ ᎤᎾᎾ Sally Bull ᎤᎾᎾ ᏥᏛᏁᎲ Ꮎ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏃᏭ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏛᏳᏅᏛᏅᏒ 51 ᏥᏭᏂᎶᏒ ᏃᏭᏂ Ꮎ ᎥᏅᏛᏅᏍᎩ ᏧᏅᎨᏛᏕᎳ. ᎠᏯᏃᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏝᏲ ᏱᏛᎬᏛᏅᏏ ᏝᏲ ᏱᏛᎬᎨᎯᏙᎵ ᎬᏥᏲᎮᎸ. ᏙᏗ ᏔᎵᎭᏛ ᏂᏕᎬᎵᎲ ᏒᏅᏙᏓᏩᏍᏗ. ᎭᏓᏅᏂ ᎤᎾᎢ ᎬᏬᏎᎲ ᏕᎨᏨᎴ ᏛᏯᏩᏂᏔᏲ ᎬᎩᎯᏍᏗ ᏙᏗᏲᏨᏟ ᎮᏂᏲ ᏝᏛᏲ ᏴᏃᏭ ᏛᏛᏅᏍᏛᏲ Sam ᏛᏃ ᎭᏓᏅᏂ ᎤᎾᎢ Ꮟ ᏂᎨᏨᎸᏄᏭ ᎩᎫᏛ ᏃᏭ ᏣᎬᏗ ᏣᏬᏎᎸ. ᏙᎯᏳᏛ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏝᏛᏲ ᏯᏂᎩᏔᎮ ᏧᎾᎵᏍᏗᏲ ᏝᏙ ᎣᏍᏗ ᏗᏍᏈᏂ ᎬᏗ Ᏺ ᎨᎲ ᏱᎨᏣᏂᎮᏂᏲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏯᎾᏁᎵᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏕᎬᏥᏴᏂᏏᎶᏍᎬ ᎾᎩᏤᎲ ᏱᎨᎲ ᏦᏛ ᏃᏍᏛᏟᎲ ᏌᏊ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏒᏂᏙᏓᏩᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ. ᎣᎩᏂᏍᏛᏛᎲᏍᎬ. ᎠᎮᏃᏲ ᏝᏍᏊᏲ ᎠᏧᏣᏭᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏯᏂᏲ ᎣᏍᏗ ᎮᏂᏴᏅ ᏗᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ ᏧᎷᏨ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎩᏗ “ᏙᎲᏟᎮᏧ” ᎾᏅ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏩᏥᎨᎯᏙᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎠᏯᎾ Ꮟ ᏓᏩᏨᏙ ᏧᏩᏩᏛᏅᏒ ᏝᏴ ᏧᏩᎬᏲᎵᎸ
segments.transliteration: noheni Salemi nav tsineli esditliyv CC campi utliditli una tsineli hisgi dvno nadetiyv una gvgilutsv unana naheni wugediliyv tsigev unana Sally Bull unana tsidvnehv na vgido agvyi nowu una tsidvyunvdvnvsv 51 tsiwunilosv nowuni na vnvdvnvsgi tsunvgedvdela. ayanowu tsigehv tlayo yidvgvdvnvsi tlayo yidvgvgehidoli gvtsiyohelv. dodi talihadv nidegvlihv svnvdodawasdi. hadanvni unai gvwosehv degetsvle dvyawanitayo gvgihisdi dodiyotsvtli heniyo tladvyo yvnowu dvdvnvsdvyo Sam dvno hadanvni unai si nigetsvlvnuwu gigudv nowu tsagvdi tsawoselv. dohiyudv aseno tladvyo yanigitahe tsunalisdiyo tlado osdi disquini gvdi yo gehv yigetsaniheniyo tsigehv yananelidi gehv sgidv degvtsiyvnisilosgv nagitsehv yigehv tsodv nosdvtlihv saquu atsutsa svnidodawasdi gehv. oginisdvdvhvsgv. ahenoyo tlasquuyo atsutsawuni sgina ayaniyo osdi heniyvnv didaniyisgi tsulutsv saquu yuwagidi “dohvtlihetsu” nanv tsiyohelv watsigehidolv na atsutsa ayana si dawatsvdo tsuwawadvnvsv tlayv tsuwagvyolilv
segments.translation: I lived before in Salem and past CC Camp, I lived there for five years, that’s where my sister used to live, down Sally Bull Holler before they moved out to 51. When those users had taken over that area I lived there, I told them, “I’m not going to leave there, they aren’t going to run me off.” I used to get into two fights in one week. They used to tell me, “Move out of there, they’re going to kill you.” I told them, “They aren’t going to kill me, we’re going to fight.” You’re going to have to move one of these days, and Sam told me, “You better move, you got blood on your face.” But they don’t know how to fight, not with fists anyway. They tried to grab me, but I’d punch them repeatedly. I used to get in a fight three times with that one boy in one week. We were having disagreements and he was just a young man, and I was older. One day the cops showed up. They said, “Have you been fighting again?” and made him leave and I was still in charge. Eventually I moved, because I got tired of it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏫᏓᏣᏯᏪᏤᏭᎲ ᏕᎲᏂᎵᏙᎲ ᏫᏨᏛᏅᏎᏫᎲ ᏃᏭ
segments.transliteration: widatsayawetsewuhv dehvnilidohv witsvdvnvsewihv nowu
segments.translation: So, you got tired of fighting and just moved away?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏙᏛ ᎾᏛ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎥᏂᏛᏅᏍᎩ ᏢᎮ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏗᎩᏙᏗ ᏱᎩ ᏗᏅᏗᏔᏍᎩ ᏧᏂᏴᏍᏕᏗ ᏫᏍᎩ ᏯᏂᏥᏙ ᏲᎮᏂ ᎤᏬᏟᏚᏲ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎰ *mumbles*
segments.transliteration: dodv nadv gohusdi vnidvnvsgi tlvhe gohusdi digidodi yigi dinvditasgi tsuniyvsdedi wisgi yanitsido yoheni uwotliduyo heni geho *mumbles*
segments.translation: Yeah, those users aren’t worth a thing, and they’d just be drinking, and getting drunk. If they got whiskey, they’d be laughing around like it isn’t nothing.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎤᎾᏍ ᎦᏚᏏ ᏣᏕᏁ ᎤᎾ ᏣᏕᏁ
segments.transliteration: unas gadusi tsadene una tsadene
segments.translation: Were you born on the mountain? (Referring to Oak Ridge)

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎤᎾ Boss ᏥᎦᏁᎸ Ꮟ ᎯᏗᏝ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎦᎾᏩ ᏗᏝ ᎤᎾᏛᏲ ᏙᎦᏛᏒ ᏲᎨᎲ ᎦᏚᏏ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍ- Oak Ridge ᏣᏓᏁᎵ Ꮟ ᎾᏂᎨ ᎤᎾᎮᏂ Ꮩ ᏙᏦᎦᏛᏒ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv una Boss tsiganelv si hiditla gehv uganawa ditla unadvyo dogadvsv yogehv gadusi gohitsigi tsunilawis- Oak Ridge tsadaneli si nanige unaheni do dotsogadvsv gehv
segments.translation: Yeah, by where boss used to live, to the south, that’s where we grew up. Right about where that house is at Oak Ridge, right in there is where we grew up.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭᎨ ᏗᏣᏛᏏᏙᎸ ᎭᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: yudahage ditsadvsidolv hadanvtesgo
segments.translation: Do you reminisce about where you grew up sometimes?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏪᏙᎰᏛ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏝᏃ ᏯᏓᏁᎵ ᏃᏭ ᏝᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᎠᎹᎵᏗᎮᏂ ᏣᏔᎴᏒᏲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎩᏗ Ꮎ ᏅᏱ ᎦᏗ ᏥᏓᏐᏴ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ Ꮎ ᎯᎸᏍᎩᏄᎲ ᏧᏩᏪᏙᎸᏭ ᎤᎧᏲᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎸᎯᏳ ᎤᎶᏒ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏍᎩ ᏂᏙᏓᎦᎵᏍᏔᏂ ᎠᏅᏗᏍᎨ ᎮᏂᏲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎢᏥᏑᎸᎪᏨ ᎢᏣᏗᏍᎬ ᎯᎠ ᎠᎹᎵᏗ ᏛᎧᏲᏏ. ᎤᏠᏱ Ꮎ ᎥᏓᎵ ᏥᏓᏃᏢᏍᎬ ᏩᎦ ᏧᏂᎾᏝ ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏒ ᎠᏭᏗᏝ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏬᎦᏓᏬᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏩᎦ ᏥᏚᏂᏅᎪᏫᏐᏅ ᏥᏚᏅᏛᏅᏐᏅ ᏴᏫ. ᎤᎧᏲᏗ ᏃᏭ. ᎢᎪᎯᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎢᏨᏗᎲ ᏄᏍᏕᏍᏗᏭ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ. Ꮩ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏂᏌᎹᏗ ᎨᎮ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ ᏣᏁᎲ ᎨᎵᎰ.
segments.transliteration: wedohodv nigohilv yusdi aseno tlano yadaneli nowu tlalvhiyu awadelahosv yusdi yigehe nigalisdisgv amalidiheni tsatalesvyo osda yigidi na nvyi gadi tsidasoyv sgi tsinusdv na hilvsginuhv tsuwawedolvwu ukayodi tsigehv tla lvhiyu ulosv yigehe aseno sgi nidodagalistani anvdisge heniyo tsigehv itsisulvgotsv itsadisgv hia amalidi dvkayosi. utloyi na vdali tsidanotlvsgv waga tsuninatla tsidegotlvsv awuditla nigohilv wogadawosdi tsigehv. waga tsiduninvgowisonv tsidunvdvnvsonv yvwi. ukayodi nowu. igohidi gohusdi itsvdihv nusdesdiwu anadisge tsigehv. do squu anisamadi gehe anigayvli tsanehv geliho.
segments.translation: Yeah, I go back there but where I grew up, that house isn’t there anymore. I never could figure it out, but that well we had, had rocks around it. I went back over there a few days ago, I looked in there and it was dry. It had never done that when we were living there, but they used to say if you’re not using that well, it’s going to dry up. It’s just like those ponds those ranchers used to build. We used to go up there and swim in them, but when they moved their cows, they dried up. They would dry up, but they used to say, “If you’re not using something, it’s going to go away.” The elders really knew what they were talking about.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᎾᏔᏅᏛ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: unatanvdv anigayvli tsigehv
segments.translation: The Elders back then.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎾᎮᏂ Covid ᏧᎯᎶᏢ Ꮎ ᎣᎩᎦᏘ, ᎡᏦᎵᎩᏛ Jerry Nofire? ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏭᏟᏗᏟᏴ ᏔᎵ ᎠᏎ ᏦᎢ ᎴᏱᎩ ᎾᏕᏘᏴ Ꮟ ᎾᎯᎶᎯᎲᏂ ᎠᎦᏍᎩᏏᏍᏔᏁ ᏧᏛᏅ ᎪᎱᏍᏗᏕ ᏛᎯᎵ ᎢᏣᎦᏎᏍᏕᏍᏗ. ᏴᏫ ᏙᏓᎩᏲᎱᏎᎵ ᎠᏬᏎᎸ ᎠᎩᏍᎩᏒ ᏧᏛᏅ ᏦᎢ ᏫᏄᏕᏘᏴ Ꮭ ᎣᏂ ᏧᎯᎶᏢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏧᎾᎴᏅᎲ ᏴᏫ ᎠᏅᏒᎲᏍᎬ ᎦᏳᎵ ᏧᏅᏛ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏝᏲ ᏳᎾᏖ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎯᎶᏟᏒ ᎨᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏕᏲ ᏓᏯᎢ ᏧᏛᏅ
segments.transliteration: naheni Covid tsuhilotlv na ogigati, etsoligidv Jerry Nofire? sginana wutliditliyv tali ase tsoi leyigi nadetiyv si nahilohihvni agasgisistane tsudvnv gohusdide dvhili itsagasesdesdi. yvwi dodagiyohuseli awoselv agisgisv tsudvnv tsoi winudetiyv tla oni tsuhilotlv sgina gohusdi tsunalenvhv yvwi anvsvhvsgv gayuli tsunvdv sgina tlayo yunate yusdi dihilotlisv gehv gohusdeyo dayai tsudvnv
segments.translation: When COVID came through our pastor, you guys know Jerry Nofire, he was given a dream, and he was told that something is going to come and something’s going to happen and we’re all going to lose people. Three years later, it came, people started passing. He knew something was coming, but he didn’t know quite what it was.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᎢᎦᏗ ᏛᏙ ᎨᏥᏅᎪᏫᏎᎲ. ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮭ ᏱᎨᏥᏃᏎᎮ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏓᎬᎷᏣ
segments.transliteration: yeah, igadi dvdo getsinvgowisehv. asena tla yigetsinosehe yusdi gehv asena tsadihv. dagvlutsa
segments.translation: Yeah, some did have a revelation. They didn’t know quite what was going to happen, but they knew something was going to happen.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎠᏥᏃᏎᎮ, ᎠᏯ ᎮᎾ ᏥᎦ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᏅ ᎮᏂ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏩᏕᏟᏗ. ᎦᏳᎵᏧ ᏫᏙᎲᏓᎴᏍᏗ ᏴᏬᏏ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏕᏥᎳᏫᏥᏙ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏳᏫ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏗᏩᏓᎴᏍᏙᏗ ᏩᏥᏅᎩᎬ ᏌᏭ Ꮫ ᏱᎾᎩᏅᏗ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏱᎠᎩᎷᏥ ᎦᏳᎵᎢᏧ ᏫᏙᎲᏓᎴᏍᏗ ᏯᏬᏏ ᎨᎲ. ᎲᎥ ᏏᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᏗᏲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏬᎮᎲ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏥᎯᏄᎪᏥ ᏣᏬᏎᎲ. ᏝᏲ ᏗᏩᏁᏟᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏝᏲ ᏱᏥᏅᎪᎨ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎨᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: atsinosehe, aya hena tsiga aginulvnv heni gusda awadetlidi. gayulitsu widohvdalesdi yvwosi heni tsigehv detsilawitsido asena yuwi heni gehv gusda diwadalesdodi watsinvgigv sawu dv yinaginvdi tsunilawisdi yiagilutsi gayuliitsu widohvdalesdi yawosi gehv. hvv sidv osda tsiyohehv diyo osda yiga awohehv. asena hesdi tsihinugotsi tsawosehv. tlayo diwanetlidi yigehe asena tlayo yitsinvgoge nigolv heni gedohv
segments.translation: I can’t keep a secret. They’ll usually say, “You already messed it up.” I try to go to church but sometimes I mess up, and if I miss church one time, they’ll usually say, “Gaw, you messed up again?” I’d say, “No I’m still good.” I’m not religious, but I still go.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏏᎨ ᏥᎦ ᎤᎾ ᎮᏙᎰ?
segments.transliteration: sige tsiga una hedoho?
segments.translation: Do you still go there?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏅᎩᏍᎪ ᏛᏢ ᎾᏕᏘᏱ ᏂᎨᏙᎰ ᎤᎾ
segments.transliteration: v, nvgisgo dvtlv nadetiyi nigedoho una
segments.translation: Yeah, I’ve been going there for about 40 years.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎦᎪ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎪ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ ᎤᎾ?
segments.transliteration: gago alitsidohvsgo gohiyv tsiga una?
segments.translation: Who preaches over there now?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: bull,
segments.transliteration: bull,
segments.translation: Bull.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏏᏍᎪᏅ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ?
segments.transliteration: sisgonv atsalagiha?
segments.translation: All Cherokee?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎡᏧᎳ, ᎾᏛ ᎣᏂ ᏧᎾᏛᏒ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᏯᏃᎵᎬ ᎾᏭᏅ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ Ꮭ ᎮᏂ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏃᎵᎬ ᏱᎦ ᎡᎵᏍᏕ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᏯᏃᏟᎩ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎬ ᏝᏅ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᏃᎵᎬ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏂᏯ
segments.transliteration: etsula, nadv oni tsunadvsv hesdi heni atsalagi yanoligv nawunv agvyi anigayvli tla heni gusda anoligv yiga elisde atsalagi yanotligi alitsidohvsgv tlanv gusdi anoligv yiga aniya
segments.translation: No, both, cause the younger ones don’t understand Cherokee, but the older ones don’t understand anything. They should understand Cherokee, but they still don’t understand Anything.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᏧᎾᏁᏟᏗ ᎤᎾᏓᏢᎬ ᏕᏥᎦᏘᏯ Kenwood ᏗᏝ steele ᎠᏃᏎᎰ. ᏳᏓᎭ ᎬᎩᏛᏛᎲᏍᎪ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭᎨ ᎭᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎪ? ᎡᏧᎳᏛ ᏗᎦᏙᏗ ᎾᏫᎵᏍᏓᏁᎰ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎢᎦᏓ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎠᏃᎵᎬ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏲᏁᎩ ᏱᎦ ᏃᎴ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎤᏱᎦ ᎠᏃᎵᎪᎡ. ᎢᎦᏗᏅ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᏃᎵᎬ ᏱᎦ ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎰ
segments.transliteration: aya heni sgu tsunanetlidi unadatlvgv detsigatiya Kenwood ditla steele anoseho. yudaha gvgidvdvhvsgo atsalagihage halitsidohvsgo? etsuladv digadodi nawilisdaneho gatsiyohehv igada atsalagiha anoligv igada yonegi yiga nole yonega uyiga anoligoe. igadinv gehv tla gohusdi anoligv yiga gatsiyoseho
segments.translation: I preach in Kenwood, at a church called Steeley. Sometimes they ask me if I preach Cherokee. I tell them sometimes I must use both, cause Cherokees understand Cherokee, and the Whites understand English. A few of them don’t even understand.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛᎮ Ꮎ ᎦᏚᏏ ᏣᏁᎭ ᏧᎾᏓᎵᎦ ᏩᎦᏔᏛ ᏍᎫ ᎯᏴᏣᏅᎯᏒ ᏥᏲᏏ Ꮫ bull ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᏱᎾᎵᏥᏙᎲᎦ. ᏗᏂᏯᏨᏅᎯᏕ ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎰ Ꮎ ᎪᎯᏓ ᎠᎾᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎦ
segments.transliteration: sgidvhe na gadusi tsaneha tsunadaliga wagatadv sgu hiyvtsanvhisv tsiyosi dv bull yigohida yinalitsidohvga. diniyatsvnvhide gatsiyoseho na gohida analitsidohvsga
segments.translation: Yeah, those that live on the mountain. I told Bull your neck keeps getting longer because you preached a long time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏃ ᏦᏍᎪ ᏯᏔᏬᏍᏛᏅ ᏯᏩᎵᏥᏙᏂ ᏃᏫᏛ ᏗᎾᎵᏟᏖᎸᎲᏍᎪ. Ꭰ ᏂᏗᏅᏛᏁᎰ Ꮂ ᏴᏩᏘ ᏚᏂᏲᏏᎲ ᏱᎦ. Ꭰ ᏥᏨᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᎠᎹᎨ Ꮎ ᎠᎾᎦᎵᏍᎦ ᏗᏨᏍᏓ ᏥᏕᎩᏨᏍᏓ ᏃᏥᎦ ᏍᎩᎨ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏂᏨᎾᏁ ᏗᏤᏅ
segments.transliteration: ayano tsosgo yatawosdvnv yawalitsidoni nowidv dinalitlitelvhvsgo. a nidinvdvneho hv yvwati duniyosihv yiga. a tsitsvdvsidisv amage na anagalisga ditsvsda tsidegitsvsda notsiga sgige yusda nitsvnane ditsenv
segments.translation: If I preach more than 30 minutes, they start getting fidgety. I don’t know if they’re just getting hungry. While you were growing up, did you have water and electricity like we have now?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏛᏲᏅ ᎠᏯ ᏙᏦᎬᏛᏒ ᏢᏲ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᏗᎾᎬᎵᏍᎦ ᏫᏚᎷᏨ ᏱᎦ ᎲᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏚᏏ ᎤᎾᏭ ᎮᏂ ᎪᎢ ᎤᏴᏟ ᏗᏟᏍᏗ ᏥᏙᎩᏨᏍᏛ ᏍᎨ ᏲᏍᏓ ᏙᏥᎧᏁ ᎨᎵᎰ ᎾᎯᏳ. ᎯᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏓᏨᏍᏗ ᏎᎦᏨ ᏥᎪᏩᏘᎰ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏕᏥᎪᎵᏰᏍᎬ. ᎾᎯᏳᏅ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏙᏥᎪᎵᏰᏍᎬ ᎨᏴ ᏃᎬᏓᎸ. ᏍᎫᏭᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏨᏍᏗ ᏣᏝᎲ ᏍᎨᎮ ᏱᏧᏍᎪᏍᏗ ᏙᏥᎧᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ
segments.transliteration: dvyonv aya dotsogvdvsv tlvyo alvhiyu dinagvlisga widulutsv yiga hvnv sgu una gadusi unawu heni goi uyvtli ditlisdi tsidogitsvsdv sge yosda dotsikane geliho nahiyu. hinv yusdi datsvsdi segatsv tsigowatiho gowela detsigoliyesgv. nahiyunv tsigesv gowela dotsigoliyesgv geyv nogvdalv. sguwunv yusdi atsvsdi tsatlahv sgehe yitsusgosdi dotsikanv nahiyu
segments.translation: Not when I was growing up. We didn’t have electricity. We used coal oil lamps. We were sitting apart, and we could see good. Up on the mountain, that’s the kind of light we had, and we could still see good. Nowadays we have good lights, and we can barely see. Back then we only had those kinds of lights, we must’ve had better Vision.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎪᏢᏎᏍ ᏧᎾᏕᎵᏆᏍᏗ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏚᏌ ᏥᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᎭᏢᎨᏴ ᏕᏣᏕᎳᏆᎡ?
segments.transliteration: gotlvses tsunadeliquasdi nahiyu una gadusa tsitsadvsidisv hatlvgeyv detsadelaquae?
segments.translation: Was there school up there where you grew up or where did you go to school?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎠᎡ ᎤᏟᏗᏟᏴ ᏑᏟᎶᏗ ᎢᎾᎨᎡ ᏛᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᏛᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ. ᎰᏩ ᎠᏪᎵᏐᏅ ᎠᎮᏂ. ᏔᏕᏠᎦ ᏢᎡᏴ ᏦᏢᏪ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏲᏢᏍᎦ ᎬᏬᎮᎸ. ᎾᎾᏩᏛᏂ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏠᎨᏌ ᎠᏰᏟ ᎠᏬᏢ ᎠᎵᎭ ᎠᏬᏢᏭᏅ ᎠᏕᎳ ᎪᏢᏍᎬ. ᎠᎮᏅ Ꮲ ᎤᏟᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏱᏚᏪᏘᏁ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ. ᏧᎾᏛᏅᏍᏛᏅ Ꮎ ᎾᏩ ᏥᎦ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏣᏓᏁᎳ ᎠᏗᏝ ᏧᎾᏁᏍᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮂ ᏱᏓᏩᏕᎳᏆᎡ ᎠᏯ. ᏧᏩᏩᏂᎩᏒ ᎡᎵᏭᏛ ᏂᏥᏌᎹᏗᏴ Ꮓ
segments.transliteration: ae utliditliyv sutlilodi inagee dvtsigehv tsunadelaquasdi dvdanelv aya heni una awalenvhv. howa awelisonv aheni. tadetloga tlveyv tsotlvwe adela yotlvsga gvwohelv. nanawadvni gatsiyohelv sawu yuwagada tlogesa ayetli awotlv aliha awotlvwunv adela gotlvsgv. ahenv tlv utliigohida yiduwetine sgina tsunadelaquasdi. tsunadvnvsdvnv na nawa tsiga tsunilawisdi tsadanela aditla tsunanesgehv asena hv yidawadelaquae aya. tsuwawanigisv eliwudv nitsisamadiyv no
segments.translation: There was a school way out in the woods. That’s where I started school, and they would try to tell me to go to school so I would have a job sitting but I was sitting in field making money all sweaty. But that school didn’t last very long. They moved it where that church is now, they built it other side of it. But I didn’t go to school there, I felt like I was smart enough.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏠᎨᏌ Ꮕ ᎠᏰᏟ ᏦᏞ, ᎠᏕᎳ ᎰᏢᏍᎦ ᎡᏦᏎᎴ
segments.transliteration: tlogesa nv ayetli tsotle, adela hotlvsga etsosele
segments.translation: You were just sitting out in the field making money?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏚᏯ ᏗᎦᏕᏍᎦ
segments.transliteration: duya digadesga
segments.translation: Yeah, picking Beans.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏥᏕᏤᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎢᏥᏑᏓᏁᎷᏭᏍ ᎢᏥᏠᎢᏴ ᏕᏤᎮ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏚᏌ
segments.transliteration: una tsidetsehe nahiyu itsisudaneluwus itsitloiyv detsehe una gadusa
segments.translation: Was it all your siblings and relatives living on the hill?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏂᎦᏗᏛ ᎣᎩᏠᎢᏴ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏚᏌ ᏦᏤᎲ
segments.transliteration: nigadidv ogitloiyv gehv una gadusa tsotsehv
segments.translation: We were all relatives living on the hill.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏏᏕᎰᏂ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ ᏙᎭ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏄᏍᏓ?
segments.transliteration: sidehoni gohiyv tsiga doha sgiheni nusda?
segments.translation: Is it still like that today?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏢᏃ ᏍᏈᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏓᎾᏁᎳᏗ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏓᏅᏘᏃᎯᎭ. ᏲᏁᎦ Ꮕ ᏥᏭᏖᎸᏛ ᏧᏮᏥᎾᏌᏅ ᏥᏭᏁᎳᏗᏢ Jim Capps ᏧᏙᎩᏓ ᎤᏁᎳᏗᏭᏛ ᏥᎦᎥᎣᏍᏛ ᏌᎷᏱ ᏗᏬᏠ. ᎤᎾᏂᎩᏏᏛᏅ ᎠᏮᏏ ᏩᏮᎵᏍᏕᎸᎲ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ Ꮫ ᏲᏥ ᏬᎦᏢᏔᎭᏅ Ꮟ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᏙᎩᏲᏒ ᎮᏂ ᏂᎦᏗ. ᎲᏃ ᏔᎵᏁ ᏲᏣᏕᏙᏛᏁ. ᏅᏱ Ꭱ ᎬᏗ ᏙᏥᏅᏗᎲ ᎤᏛᏢᏍᏛᏂ Ᏺ ᎤᏦᏙᏗ. ᎤᏩᏏ ᏅᎮ ᎤᎮ ᎤᏦᏙᏗ. ᎤᎾ ᎦᏚᏌ ᏙᎮᏂ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏭᎮᏂ ᎣᏤᏙᎲ. ᏧᏛᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᏐᏫᎵ ᏳᎶᏏ. Luck ᎤᏭᏅ ᎤᏩᏂᎲ ᏂᏥᏍᎫᏍᎬᏂ ᏱᎦ. ᏙᎮᏂ ᏢᎮᏂ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎤᎾᏓᎾᏖᏗ ᎠᏯ ᏕᎲᏂ ᎨᎸ ᎠᏎᎾ. ᎾᎮᏂ ᏦᏍᏓᏅᏟ Ꮓ boss ᏗᎾᏓᏅᏟ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎠnlᎡᏂᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎫᏍᏓ. ᎬᏩᎦᏗᏅ ᏫᎾᏅᏛᏁᎲ ᎠᏯᏅ ᏩᏣᎵᏒᏁᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎾᎴᏂᏍᎬ ᎠᏯᏅ ᏬᎬᏛᏃ ᎣᏥᏍᎬᏅᏨᎲᏍᎬ. ᎸᏢ ᏧᏂᏰᏥᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏩᎦᏛ ᏧᏂᏰᏥᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᏛᏳᎾᎴᏅᏗ ᎨᎲ. ᎾᎮᏂ bellᎢ ᏣᏁᎠ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏦᏨᏙᏟᎩ ᏱᎨᎮ. ᏢᎮᏂ ᏙᎮᏂ ᎣᏤᏙ ᏱᎨᎮ. ᏢᎮᏂ ᏲᏥᎦᏐᏍᎨ ᎦᏚᏌ ᎤᎾᏭ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏤᎰᏩᏕᎬ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏂᏙᎬᎳᏑᏢᏂ ᎯᎠᏎ ᏳᎭᎨᏗ ᏙᎦᏍᏛᏁᎬᎴ ᎨᎵᎰ. ᏌᎷᏱ ᏲᏣᎵᏝᎥᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏛᎫᏍᏓ ᎥᎸᎯᏳ ᎩᎶ ᏴᎪᏩᏗ ᏴᏱᎩᏓ ᏱᎧᎾᏒᏗ ᎤᎾᏍᏆᎶᎥ ᎤᎾᏍᏆᎶᎥᏂ. ᏙᎬᏛᏏᏌᏅ ᎮᏂ ᎩᎳ ᏦᎩᎦᏐᏒ. Ꮎ ᎦᏚᏌ ᎠᏁᎭ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᎤᏁᎳᎦ ᎨᏍᎡᏍᏗ ᏓᏃᎮᎲ bellᎢ ᎠᏁᎭ ᏙᏍᎩᏅ ᎨᎶ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎡᏚᏓ. ᏢᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ ᎢᏣᏓᏅᏖᏗ ᎦᏚᏌ ᏗᏣᏛᏒ ᏧᏛᏅ. ᏢᏭ ᎠᎮ ᏄᎾᏓᎴ ᏴᏫ ᎠᏁᏙᎲ ᏗᏣᏛᏒ ᏱᎦ ᏧᏛᏅ ᏙᏅᎮᏍᎫ ᎢᎾᎨᏭ ᎣᏤᎨᎮ. ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᏢᏯᏩᏘ ᎡᏚᏓ Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎢᎪᎯᏗ ᏛᎨᎲ ᏙᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎲᏛᎦ, ᏗᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᎦᏛᎦ ᎯᏛ ᎠᏂᏃᎮ ᎭᏢᏅ ᎤᎾ ᏱᎨᏙᎮ. ᎦᎩᏭ ᏛᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᏧᏛᏁᎳ ᎠᏯ Ꮫ ᏕᎬᎩᎧᏅ, ᎮᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎾᎩᏅᏙᏂ ᏥᎦᏥᏲᏎᎲ ᏥᏍᎬᏅᏨᎲᏍᎪᎡ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏢᏍᎩ ᏱᎦ ᏱᎦ ᏥᎦᏥᏲᏎᎲ
segments.transliteration: tlvno squisdi heni dananeladi nudale danvtinohiha. yonega nv tsiwutelvdv tsuwvtsinasanv tsiwuneladitlv Jim Capps tsudogida uneladiwudv tsigavosdv saluyi diwotlo. unanigisidvnv awvsi wawvlisdelvhv hilvsgi dv yotsi wogatlvtahanv si. asena dogiyosv heni nigadi. hvno taline yotsadedodvne. nvyi e gvdi dotsinvdihv udvtlvsdvni yo utsododi. uwasi nvhe uhe utsododi. una gadusa doheni eladi wuheni otsedohv. tsudvdi heni gehv sowili yulosi. Luck uwunv uwanihv nitsisgusgvni yiga. doheni tlvheni osda yigehe unadanatedi aya dehvni gelv asena. naheni tsosdanvtli no boss dinadanvtli utanida sgiheni anlenisgi tsigehv gusda. gvwagadinv winanvdvnehv ayanv watsalisvnegv sgina analenisgv ayanv wogvdvno otsisgvnvtsvhvsgv. lvtlv tsuniyetsisgo sgina wagadv tsuniyetsisgo sgina sgina nidvyunalenvdi gehv. naheni belli tsanea hesdi heni tsotsvdotligi yigehe. tlvheni doheni otsedo yigehe. tlvheni yotsigasosge gadusa unawu heni otsehowadegv inage nidogvlasutlvni hiase yuhagedi dogasdvnegvle geliho. saluyi yotsalitlavsdi gehv dvgusda vlvhiyu gilo yvgowadi yvyigida yikanasvdi unasqualov unasqualovni. dogvdvsisanv heni gila tsogigasosv. na gadusa aneha anitsutsa unelaga gesesdi danohehv belli aneha dosginv gelo tsiyohelv sawu yuwagada eduda. tlvnv osda yiga itsadanvtedi gadusa ditsadvsv tsudvnv. tlvwu ahe nunadale yvwi anedohv ditsadvsv yiga tsudvnv donvhesgu inagewu otsegehe. gelisgo tlvyawati eduda dv tsigehv igohidi dvgehv dousdi ahvdvga, digusda yigadvga hidv aninohe hatlvnv una yigedohe. gagiwu dvgusda yitsudvnela aya dv degvgikanv, hesdi dv sgi yinaginvdoni tsigatsiyosehv tsisgvnvtsvhvsgoe asena tlvsgi yiga yiga tsigatsiyosehv
segments.translation: We’re not all like that now, because they get married and bring different people. A white man joined us, and I robbed him. He moved in and his name was Jim Capps. I was watching and as soon as he left, I went in and helped myself. It wasn’t very long, and they caught up to me. And they let us all go. We never bothered him again. But we would throw rocks at him when he drove by. He was the only one who had a car up there, we used to just walk around. Someone was rich if they rode by on a horse. Boy, he was lucky I didn’t hit him in the head. Really, they weren’t any good. Of course, I was with them too. It was boss’s older brother; he was the one who started it all. They used to get away with it. We would get the blame for it. The rest of us would get in trouble and they would be laughing. They’re the ones that started it. Those people down Bell, we didn’t get along because we never came down. We just stayed up there in woods with no shoes on. I wonder how thick the soles of our feet were. We would run through the woods like it was nothing. Sometimes you would see someone with a toe ye big [gestures] because they stumped their toe. Where they stumped it somewhere. We didn’t go off the hill until we were older but them older boys on the hill would tell them Bell boys to leave us alone. Sometimes I wondered why and then my grandpa said, “It’s because you boys that grew up the hill don’t act right because y’all didn’t grow up around other people.” I guess we did just live in the woods. That’s what I think anyway. Sometimes my grandpa would ask, “What did you do?” They would say, “Someone did something.” They would all look at me. I’m not that foolish. Yeah, I make a lot of mistakes, but not that Bad.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏅ ᏱᎦ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᎨᎮ ᎾᎯ ᎾᎾᏃ ᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ
segments.transliteration: nana atsalagi unv yiga hiwonisgi gehe nahi nanano tsadvsidisv
segments.translation: Did you just speak Cherokee back then? What about growing up?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎤᏕᎰᎯᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎩᎶ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏱᎦᏬᏂ ᎠᏯ ᎣᎬᏏ ᎣᎦᏓᏢᎬ ᎨᎲ. ᎾᎾ ᎠᏴᏕᎾ ᎤᏤᎸ ᎠᏩ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏗᎦᏬᏂ ᏯᏅᏓᏙᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎩᎵ ᏛᎣᏂ ᏣᏩᏠᏒ ᎤᎾ ᎣᏛᎵ ᎩᎳ
segments.transliteration: udehohisdi dv tsigesv gilo yonega yigawoni aya ogvsi ogadatlvgv gehv. nana ayvdena utselv awa yonega digawoni yanvdadosi tsigehv. gili dvoni tsawatlosv una odvli gila
segments.translation: It was embarrassing back then for someone to speak English. Where my group was, they didn’t speak English. If someone did, they’d say they were acting big if they spoke English. It wasn’t until I came off the mountain.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎩᎵ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ Ꮓ ᏲᏁᎦ Ꮓ
segments.transliteration: gili sdigida no yonega no
segments.translation: Then a little English.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: Ꮓ ᎠᏎ ᏲᏁᎦ
segments.transliteration: no ase yonega
segments.translation: Now I started speaking English.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏄᎵᏍᏛ Ꮓ ᎤᏣᏘᎾ Ꮲ ᎮᏙᎲ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ
segments.transliteration: nulisdv no utsatina tlv hedohv sdigida
segments.translation: Now you were off somewhere a little.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: Ꮓ ᎤᏣᏘᎾ, greasy ᏥᏓᏩᏕᎳᏆᎥ Ꮓ ᏣᏩᎴᏅ ᏍᏗ ᎪᎵᎬ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎦᎵᏅ ᏑᏓᎵᏁ Ꮲ ᏥᏥᏯᎥ. ᎠᎮᏅ ᏏᏅ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏅᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏚᏏ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ. ᎣᎩᏍᎦᎬ ᎡᏲ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏦᎦᏢᏃᎮᏗ. ᏬᏣᏎᎮᎸ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ, ᏨᏏ Ꮫ ᏣᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎠᏯᏅ ᏙᏨᏢᏃᎮ. ᏢᏲ ᏱᏙᎩᎸᏂᎮ Ꮧ ᏱᏙᎬᏲᎩᎸᏂᎦ ᎨᎲ Ꮲ ᏱᎦᏲᎬᏢᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎫ ᏳᏚᎵ ᏦᎩᎸᏂᏍᏗ ᎡᎵ ᎮᏂ ᏂᏙᏥᏄᎸ. ᎾᎮᏂ ᎯᏯᏅᏛᏗᎰ Charlie canoe? ᎤᏛᏐᏅ
segments.transliteration: no utsatina, greasy tsidawadelaquav no tsawalenv sdi goligv yonega galinv sudaline tlv tsitsiyav. ahenv sinv tsalagiha nvsi tsigehv una gadusi tsunadelaquasdi. ogisgagv eyo tsalagiha tsogatlvnohedi. wotsasehelv dideyohvsgi, tsvsi dv tsawonihisdi hiwonisgesdi ayanv dotsvtlvnohe. tlvyo yidogilvnihe di yidogvyogilvniga gehv tlv yigayogvtlvdi gehv sgu yuduli tsogilvnisdi eli heni nidotsinulv. naheni hiyanvdvdiho Charlie canoe? udvsonv
segments.translation: Yeah, it wasn’t till then. It wasn’t until I started school at Greasy, I began to understand English a little bit. I was sixth grade when I started understanding English, but it was still Cherokee on the mountain. The school on the mountain, we were scolded for speaking Cherokee. We used to point at the teacher and say, “You speak your language and we’re talking amongst ourselves.” But we really didn’t get a whopping. Even if he did, they couldn’t whoop us because they couldn’t catch us, we were too fast. Do y’all remember Charlie Canoe? He was old man.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏍᎫ ᏱᏥᏯᏅᏛᏗ, ᏥᏯᏛᎦᏅ ᎡᏲ
segments.transliteration: tla sgu yitsiyanvdvdi, tsiyadvganv eyo
segments.translation: I don’t remember him, but I’ve heard of him.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂᏲ ᏣᏖᎳᏗ ᏙᏣᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ. ᏙᏥᏓᏲᎯᎰ ᏗᎦᏓᏲᏍᏗ ᎣᎬᎨᏫᏍᎪ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ, ᎣᏣᏓᏂᏏᏂᏙᎰ ᏢᏗ ᏱᏂᏚᏍᏕ ᎯᏄᏍᏛ ᏧᏲᏣᏃᏅ ᏙᎬᏛᏂᏏᏂᏙᎸ. ᏃᎴ ᏧᏂᎨᎯᏙᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏙᎨᏲᏅ ᎪᎯᏗ ᏍᎫ. Watt bear ᏧᏙᎩᏓ ᏃᎴ ᏥᏙᎨᏲᏅ. ᏍᏛᏲ ᏡᎦ ᏗᎦᎵᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ. ᏡᎬ ᏙᏥᎵᏙᎰ tag ᏙᏣᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ. ᏙᎠᏎ monkey ᎤᎠᎮ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎮ ᎠᎾᏓᏙᏗᎰ Ꮠ ᏡᎬ ᏩᏂᏖᎳᏛᎪ watt bear ᎢᎾ ᎣᏂᏭ. ᎠᎮᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏫᏙᏨᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᏳᏬᎩᏑᎳᎪᏥ ᏙᏨᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: sgi heni dideyohvsgi tsigehv atsalaginv sgina. sgi heniyo tsateladi dotsanelohvsgv. dotsidayohiho digadayosdi ogvgewisgo tsunadelaquasdi, otsadanisinidoho tlvdi yinidusde hinusdv tsuyotsanonv dogvdvnisinidolv. nole tsunigehidolv sgina nudale dogeyonv gohidi sgu. Watt bear tsudogida nole tsidogeyonv. sdvyo tluga digalido tsigehv sgina dideyohvsgi. tlugv dotsilidoho tag dotsanelohvsgv. doase monkey uahe yusdi gehe anadadodiho so tlugv waniteladvgo watt bear ina oniwu. ahenv osda widotsvdelaquasgv yuwogisulagotsi dotsvdelaquasgv
segments.translation: He was a teacher, and he was Cherokee. He would join us sometimes and shoot marbles. And we forgot about school. We would be crawling around. There was nothing here [gesturing to knees of pants]. They were torn from crawling around chasing marbles. Then they ran him off and someone else taught us for a long time. A man named Watt Bear taught us. He used to be a tree climber. He used to climb trees and play tag. We used to climb in those trees playing tag. We were just like monkeys. We would dive off and Watt Bear would be right behind us. Then we’d have good schooling after we got done playing.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏏᎮ ᏩᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎢᏣᏛᏁᎸᏅ
segments.transliteration: sihe wanvdadisgo yudaha itsadvnelvnv
segments.translation: So, you think about what y’all did back in them days, huh?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏛᏲ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎠᏩᏅᏘ ᏗᎾᎬᎵᏍᎦ ᏥᏂᏕᎬᏅ ᎩᎵ ᎮᏂᏴ ᏓᎩᎪᎲ ᏗᎾᎬᎵᏍᎦ
segments.transliteration: una dvyo uwasa awanvti dinagvlisga tsinidegvnv gili heniyv dagigohv dinagvlisga
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s the only place I knew that had electricity. That was the first time I remember seeing electricity.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: una tsunadelaquasdi
segments.translation: At that school.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏥᏓᏂᏏᎳᏛᏍᎬ ᏢᎮ ᏯᏩᏖ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏄᏰᏟᏛ. ᏓᏂᏏᎵᏛᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎩᎶ ᏗᏨᏍᏓ ᏱᏂᏚᏩᏂ ᎩᎶᏫᏛᏴ ᏙᏨᏢᏕᎮ ᎤᏯᏅᏭ Ꮫ ᏳᏬᎦᏓᎢᎾ ᏔᎵ ᏓᏏᎸᎥᏛ ᎠᏥᎳ ᏳᏩᎵᎪᏛᏂ ᏳᏕᎦᏠᏐᏂ
segments.transliteration: tsidanisiladvsgv tlvhe yawate yusdi nuyetlidv. danisilidvsgv na gilo ditsvsda yiniduwani gilowidvyv dotsvtlvdehe uyanvwu dv yuwogadaina tali dasilvvdv atsila yuwaligodvni yudegatlosoni
segments.translation: Yeah. They were putting up line, and I really didn’t know why. If someone had lights, we’d put them out. We would throw a wire up there across two wires and sparks would fly, and all the lights would go out.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮩ ᏍᏊ ᎢᏣᏓᎪᏨ ᎨᎮ
segments.transliteration: do squu itsadagotsv gehe
segments.translation: Man, you guys were mean back then.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎤᎾᏓᎪᏨ ᎡᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏱᎨᎴ
segments.transliteration: unadagotsv egehv aya heni tla gohusdi yigele
segments.translation: They were mean, I Wasn’t.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎦᏚᏌ ᏥᏤᎲ ᏥᏃᎮᏍᎬ Ꮓ ᏥᏓᏨᏠᏒ. ᎢᎳᏯᎨ ᎢᏣᏂᏍᏓᏂᏙᎴ ᎤᎾᏅ ᎡᎳᏓ ᎠᏁᏙ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎠᎾᎴᏂᏙ Ꮓ ᏥᏓᏨᏠᏒ
segments.transliteration: na gadusa tsitsehv tsinohesgv no tsidatsvtlosv. ilayage itsanisdanidole unanv elada anedo nusda analenido no tsidatsvtlosv
segments.translation: So, when y’all were back off the mountain. Did y’all have a hard time with how people were that lived down there?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, ᎣᏍᏚᏭ ᏥᏙᎬᏙᎵᏨ
segments.transliteration: hvv, osduwu tsidogvdolitsv
segments.translation: No, we got along OK.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓᏭ Ꭾ ᏕᏣᏙᎵᏤ?
segments.transliteration: osdawu he detsadolitse?
segments.translation: Y'all got along Alright.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏃᏛ ᏦᎬᎴᏅᎲ ᏙᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎵᏙᎲ Ꮎ ᏙᏨᏖᎵᏕᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏢᏅ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏅᎰᏩ ᏧᏯᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏙᏨᏁᎲ western Arkansas ᏗᏂᎶᎩᏍᎦ ᏕᎪᎩᎾᏢᏍᎬ ᏧᏯᏅ ᏱᎦ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏃᎴᏅ ᏐᏫᎳ ᎤᏂᏳᏍᏗ ᎧᏁᏍᎦ ᏧᏂᏗ ᏙᏥᏅᎬᎵᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎪᎬᏈᏴᎡᎲ ᏧᏛᎴᏅᎲ Ꮓ ᏗᏦᏙᏗ ᏙᎩᏩᏍᎬ. ᏭᏟᎯ Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏬᎬᎴᏅᎲ ᏙᏣᏗᏔᏍᎬ. ᎠᎮᏅ ᎸᏢ ᎮᏂ ᎲᎮᏂ ᎩᎶ ᏲᎦᏕᏙᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎠᏁᎸᎾᏃ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏐ bellᎢ ᎠᏁ ᎣᏍᏓᏭᎮᏂ ᏙᎦᏠᏒ
segments.transliteration: nodv tsogvlenvhv dogilvwisdanelidohv na dotsvtelidehv sgina tlvnv gusdi nvhowa tsuyanv osda nidotsvnehv western Arkansas dinilogisga degoginatlvsgv tsuyanv yiga gusda nolenv sowila uniyusdi kanesga tsunidi dotsinvgvlisgv osda gogvquiyvehv tsudvlenvhv no ditsododi dogiwasgv. wutlihi dv tsigehv no nahiyu una heni wogvlenvhv dotsaditasgv. ahenv lvtlv heni hvheni gilo yogadedodi tsigehv asena anelvnano na aniso belli ane osdawuheni dogatlosv
segments.translation: Then we started working and we used to join in with them. We used to fix wires over in western Arkansas. Farmers used to hire us for fixing fences or building horse corrals, and hay barns and they used to pay us pretty good. Then we started to buy cars and then it got worse because we started drinking. But nobody really bothered us because we were hanging out together with them boys from Bell.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓᏭ ᏕᏣᎣᎵᏤ, Ꮭ ᏱᏗᏨᏂᎵᏙᎮᏃ
segments.transliteration: osdawu detsaolitse, tla yiditsvnilidoheno
segments.translation: So y’all didn’t fight.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏗᏛᏭ ᎣᏤᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: osdidvwu otsedohv
segments.translation: No, we got along.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏓ ᏓᏩᎴᎳ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏣᎩᏌ, Ꮲ ᏯᏛᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: dohv usda dawalela agvyi tsagisa, tlv yadvdi yusdi gehv
segments.translation: Do you remember what kind of car you first Bought?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎯᎩᏍᎩᎯ ᎪᏢᏅ ford
segments.transliteration: higisgihi gotlvnv ford
segments.translation: ‘53 Ford.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᎯᏗᏅ ᏣᏕᎳᏆᎡ ᏣᎯᎸᏍᏗ?
segments.transliteration: ahidinv tsadelaquae tsahilvsdi?
segments.translation: Did you learn to drive easy?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏠᎨᏏ Ꮫ ᎠᏰᏟ ᏧᏕᎬᎩᏲᏒ. ᏔᏕᎳᏆᏛ ᏐᎢᎾ ᎨᎲ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏛᎭᏂᎩᏌ ᏧᏛᏅ. ᎾᏅ ᎠᏂᏐ ᏭᎾᏦᏛᏅ ᏭᎾᏂᎩᏒ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏥᎬᎩᏁᎸ Ꮎ car ᏠᎨᏏ. ᎡᎮᏂ Texas ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏠᎨᏏ ᎠᏰᏟ ᎠᏎᎾ automatic hᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꭰ ᏠᎨᏌ ᏬᎦᏣᏩᏗᏒ Ꮂ ᏯᏩᏅᏖ ᏄᏰᏟᏛ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏴᏬᎩᎷᏥ ᎩᎳ ᎯᎡᏍ car ᏂᎯ ᏣᏤᎵ. ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏍᏚᎢᏍᏓ ᏭᏠᏒ, ᎠᎩᏚᏣ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ Ꮠ ᏗᎲ ᏭᏣᏅ ᏔᏕᎵᏆ ᏣᎯᎸᏍᏗ ᎢᎾ ᎨᎲ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏛᎭᏂᎩᏌ ᎠᏬᎧᎮᎸ ᏭᎾᏣᏅ ᎤᎾᏂᎩᏒ ᎠᏯᏅ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏬᏢ. ᏙᏅ ᏛᎬᏕᏁᎵ ᎨᎵᎲ. ᎲᏅ ᏱᏥᎦᏔᎮ Ꮎ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏗᏮᏗ. ᏝᎦ ᎠᏩᏣᎥ ᎤᏍᏆᏃᏴᎬ ᎦᏏᏅᏍᏗᏅ ᎠᏭᏛᎸᏁ. ᎩᎶᏛ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᎠᏩᏏᏅᏒ ᏃᎴ ᏮᏩᎴᏫᏍᏛᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎰ. ᎪᎯᏴ ᎩᎳ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏩᏩᏂᎩᏒ ᎡᎵᏅ ᏥᏳᎦᏗ ᎦᏗᏝ ᎨᎵᎲ ᏍᎫᏅ ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎲ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᏆᎥ ᎠᏎᎾ Ᏺ ᎣᏏ ᎨᎲ ᏅᏃ ᏂᏛᎩᏲᏒᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏅᏃ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏛᎩᏲᏎ ditchᎢ ᎮᎾ ᏳᏩᏩᏕᎵᏤ. ᎾᏛ ᏚᏕᎵᏍᎬᎸᎲ ᏗᎦᏅᎦᎵᏍᎦ ᏯᏅᏗ ᏛᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎮᏂ Billy soap ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏛ ᏛᎦᏅᏗᏒ ᏅᏃ ᎤᏂᎪᏗ ᎮᏂ Ꮲ ᏯᏂᎦᏔᎮ ᎤᏂᎯᎸᏍᏗ Aban ᏚᏙᎥ Nathaniel Teehee ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏯᎦᏔᎮ ᎤᎯᎸᏍᏗ. ᎬᏩᎦᏗ ᎠᏎ Ꮲ ᏳᏕᎳᏆᎡ
segments.transliteration: tlogesi dv ayetli tsudegvgiyosv. tadelaquadv soina gehv eladi dvhanigisa tsudvnv. nanv aniso wunatsodvnv wunanigisv sgiheni tsigvginelv na car tlogesi. eheni Texas heni tsigehv tlogesi ayetli asena automatic hheni tsigehv sgina a tlogesa wogatsawadisv hv yawanvte nuyetlidv unanv yvwogilutsi gila hies car nihi tsatseli. ahani disduisda wutlosv, agidutsa heni gehv so dihv wutsanv tadeliqua tsahilvsdi ina gehv eladi dvhanigisa awokahelv wunatsanv unanigisv ayanv una awotlv. donv dvgvdeneli gelihv. hvnv yitsigatahe na gusda diwvdi. tlaga awatsav usquanoyvgv gasinvsdinv awudvlvne. gilodv igohida awasinvsv nole wvwalewisdvnv sgi nigalisdiho. gohiyv gila osda wawanigisv elinv tsiyugadi gaditla gelihv sgunv nigadvnehv awadelaquav asena yo osi gehv nvno nidvgiyosvna tsigehv. nvno heni yidvgiyose ditchi hena yuwawadelitse. nadv dudelisgvlvhv diganvgalisga yanvdi dvtsigehv naheni Billy soap tsigehv asedv dvganvdisv nvno unigodi heni tlv yanigatahe unihilvsdi Aban dudov Nathaniel Teehee hesdi heni yagatahe uhilvsdi. gvwagadi ase tlv yudelaquae
segments.translation: It was in Texas in the middle of a field. It was an automatic then. We were driving in the middle of a field, and I didn’t know why. They all got in and my uncle threw me the keys and said, “You’re going to learn to drive or you’re going to walk home.” They got in and left and I was sitting there. I thought “What am I going to do? I didn’t know how to drive.” I got in and it was idling for a little bit. I put it in reverse, and I backed up for a long way. Then I stopped, I kept doing that then I took off forward. “As long as I’m going the right way.” I thought. And that’s how I learned to drive. It’s a good thing they didn’t turn me loose on the road. If they’d have done that, I’d be sitting in a ditch somewhere. They would say, “There’s that ditch cleaner, ol’ Billy Soap, he was going to miss the road.” A lot of them didn’t know how to drive. Nathaniel Teehee didn’t know how to drive either. I don’t think he ever learned how to drive.

segments.text: ᏌᎶᎵᏍ ᏣᏃᎮᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᏌᎶᎵᏍ ᏚᏙᎡ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎨᏏ ᎨᎮ
segments.transliteration: salolis tsanohehv sgina. salolis dudoe nudale gesi gehe
segments.translation: Did they call him Squirrel? Was his name Squirrel, or was it someone else?

segments.text: ᏄᏓᎴ

segments.text: ᏌᎶᎵᏛ Ꮭ ᎮᏂ ᏴᏫ ᏱᎨᎮ. Ꮩ ᎮᏅᏲ ᏐᎶᎵ ᎨᎲ. ᎣᎩᏚᏥᏅ Ꮟ ᏧᏮᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾᏅ. ᏙᏳ ᎮᏂ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᎦᎯᏃᎯᏌ ᎤᏩᏏᏅ ᏍᎫ Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᎦᏣᏃᎯᏌ. ᏱᏣᏃᏎᎸᏍ ᎡᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏱᏓᏤᏞ ᎮᏂ Ꮎ wall Ꭲ ᏳᏝᏃᎮᏕ. ᏢᎮᏂ ᏲᏣᏛᏓᏍᏗᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᎾᏛ ᎠᏂ teehee ᏂᎦᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏚᏏ ᏧᎾᏓᎴᏅ. ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏯ ᎡᎵᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꭰ step ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ Chulio step ᏚᏙᎥ. ᎤᏛᏐᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ boy ᏗᎦᎾᏰᎦ ᏛᏲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎡᏚᏓ ᎨᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏙ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎡᎵᏌ ᏥᎩᎲ. ᏗᎾᏓᎸ ᎮᏂ ᏐᎢ ᏣᎡᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏌᎶᎵ ᏣᏗ ᎤᏥ ᏥᏴᏂᏏ ᏚᏙᎥ. ᏍᎫ ᎮᏂ ᏦᎢ ᏯᏂ ᎠᏩᏘ Ꮩ ᎤᎾ ᎤᎾᏓᎴᏅ ᎨᎲ. ᏢᏲ ᏯᏩᏘ ᎤᎾ ᏧᎾᏓᎴᏅ ᎤᏟᏗᏝ ᎨᎲ. ᎠᎮᏅ ᎠᏯ ᎡᎵᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꭰ step ᎮᏅ ᏳᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎨᎲ. ᎾᏅ ᎡᏚᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ vian ᎮᏅ Ꮲ ᏗᏁ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᎾᏓᏛᏂ ᎡᏚᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏲᎮᏂ Ꮲ ᏳᏓᎳ ᏧᏥᏯᎧᎲᏍᎬ. ᏒᎾᏛᏓᏩᏍᏗ Ꮲ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᏃᎴ ᏧᏩᏥᏯᏂᏍᎬ. ᎠᎮᏂ Ꮲ ᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᏗᎪᎵᏤ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏴᏫ. ᎩᎶᏭ ᎮᏂ ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᏳᏥᏯᎧᎲᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏣᎾᏖᏍᏗ ᎮᎡ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎢᏣᏓᏛᏂ, Ꮂ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏯᏩᎦᏎᏍᏕ ᎠᏂᎨᏯ ᏕᏥᎦᏖᏃᎲ

segments.translation: Squirrel wasn’t human, he really was a squirrel. He was our uncle too. You couldn’t tell him nothing, but he couldn’t tell us nothing either, cause if he did, he’d have been better off talking to that wall because we didn’t listen to him either. All those Teehees came from the mountain, but my grandma was a Step. Julio Step was my grandpa. He was scary, that was my grandpa, my grandma’s brother, and there was another that was my grandma’s sister, and that was Squirrel’s mom, Tsiyvnsdi was her name. Those were the only three that I know of, that were born there, I don’t know where they came from beyond that. My grandma was a Step, but my grandpa, I think his kinfolk were from Vian, cause every now and then I would take him over there, for about a week and then I’d go get him. I never did get to know them well, and he’d say, “Just know these are your kinfolk,” and I’d really be looking around for some women too.

ᎠᎮᏅ ᏩᎦᏛᏭ ᎠᎾᏏᏁᎬ ᎣᏣᏏᏁᎬ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏂᏐ ᏢᏴᏃ ᎣᎬᏑᏭ ᏬᎦᏟᎢᎶᏢ Burt scraper ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎾᏅᎪᏨ boy ᏍᎩᎨᏅᏲ ᎤᏍᎦᏎᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏟᏰᏗ ᎤᏙᏗ. Fiddle ᏧᏁᏟᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᎭᏢᏅ ᏣᏕᎳᏆᎡ ᏥᏥᏲᏎᎲ? California ᏧᏛᏅ ᎤᎾᏛᎨ ᏧᏛᏅ ᎠᏯᏅ ᎰᏩ ᏮᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᎠᏫᏅᏴ ᎦᏙ ᏂᏓᏳᏄᎪᏨ ᎨᎮ ᎠᏫᏅ Lyon switch ᎾᎠ ᎤᏛᏒ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏢᏴ ᎩᎳ ᏩᏮᏕᎳᎰᏒ.

California tsudvnv unadvge tsudvnv ayanv howa wvgelisgv awinvyv gado nidayunugotsv gehe awinv Lyon switch naa udvsv gehe sgina tlvyv gila wawvdelahosv.
segments.translation: I used to, but I broke my finger. I bit too hard on a hamburger. No, I smashed my fingers bad, and I couldn’t play guitar after that. All the time, we used to have guitars where we used to live, and we all gathered in the evenings, and we would sing in Cherokee. There was an old man up there named Columbus Pritchett, my aunt’s husband. He used to teach us and tell us how to behave. Every evening we would sing church songs. And then I would start singing country and western and I would mess everything up and then I’d be all by myself again. But it was good though. But in time people would back away and after a while it was just us. Burt Scraper showed up. Boy he was a good fiddle player. “Where did you learn that?” I asked him. He said, “California, that’s where I’m from.” Man, I really believed him too. He just came out of the ground over there. He was born by Lyon Switch. I found that out one day.

segments.translation: Yeah, in California. He grew up in Lyon Switch. There were some musicians that lived out in the woods back then. Sometimes they’d get together, even on the side of the road. It wasn’t electric back then like those speakers that they have now. It was standard (acoustic) guitars. They used to have something back then, I don’t know where they got it, because it was them boys from Nicut, they called it an accordion.

segments.translation: Yeah, mulberry used to grow back then, and grapes too. About everything used to grow back then. We used to just eat stuff like that back then, or we would go out and kill stuff. About anything we killed, we ate. Back then, we used to eat anything. One time we found a groundhog. It didn’t take long. We beat him up and killed him. We took him to the house. my aunt met us, and we asked her what it was. She said, “Y’all are going to know after a while when I cook him.” She took it away from us, and that’s what we ate that night. It was good to eat, but we didn’t know what it was. We used to kill raccoons too, but we knew what they were. There’s two things I’ve never ate, and I wouldn’t even eat it if I knew what it was, a skunk and a buzzard. I wouldn’t it eat it. I think sometimes they eat possums, too.

segments.translation: There was just five of us. My aunt had about 20 kids. She said, “The Bible says go replenish the earth.” I think it was at Cherry Tree, Jerry Nofire said, his wife said, “Yeah, but it didn’t tell you just to do it by yourself.” And his wife was sitting there, and they had about eight or nine kids themselves. Bull is his son. He was a third-generation preacher at Cherry Tree. But Jerry started getting sick all the time, and we knew he was going to pass soon. He said, “Y’all be thinking about who’s going to be preaching for y’all,” sometime around a year before he passed. I was talking to Bull about how he should be the one [who preaches for us], and he said, “I’ve been asking for that for a long time.” We were talking and I chose Bull, and I said, “If you agree to do so, it would be you.” He said, “Let me think about it.” And then he said, “Yeah I will, because we’re going to lose that old man before too long.” And it wasn’t about a year before he really started to get sick and going in and out of the hospital. One time he came back from the hospital, and he got on to us there at church, he said, “You guys here, you’re always praying for me to get better, it’s your fault I’m still here. I’m actually ready to leave.” He was ready to leave, it was because of us praying for him, we were trying to hang on to him. He was ready to leave, that was how he was seeing it, because his wife had already left. “Well, I can’t do anything, I have to pray for you, because that’s what you’ve been teaching us,” is what I told him. We were doing what he told us to do, but he still didn’t like it because he was wanting to go home. One day he went in, they gave up on him, there wasn’t any need for them to know, and he did go home, and then people began to gather at his house. It was like buzzards when they see something laying there. They were eating, and the old man was still hanging in there. We went to visit him, I was doing something at the church, and there was a little girl that came running over to us, she said, “Somebody wants to talk to you,” and I said, “Hang on a minute, let me finish up.” She said, “He’s sitting right there,” and when I went out, there he was after they had given up on him. We talked for a long time, and I said, “What happened?” and he said, “I didn’t feel like going home, so I just thought I better get up.” He was driving that thing that runs by itself, wheelchair. He came to the church, and he said, “I guess they ate everything up, they gave up and went home.” He lasted for about a week after that, and then we were starting to figure it out, that it was close. I visited him every day until the evening, and then one evening I left, I told him I’d come back tomorrow, but first I had to go to town, and it was about 10pm when I got back, and then the phone rang, and he had left.

segments.text: ᎠᏎᎾᏲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎮᏅ ᎣᎨᏲᏒ. ᎾᎮᏂ salemᎢ ᏣᏁᎭ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎣᏦᏝᎩ ᏱᎦ ᏯᏅᏓ ᎦᏚᏌ ᎣᏤ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᎾᎮᏂ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏂᏙᏗᎬᏅ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏙᏥᏍᏓᏩᏗ. Ꮎ ᏢᎮᏂ ᏗᎾᏓᏲᏁ ᏱᎬᏂᏴᎭ. ᎠᏯ Ꭱ ᏌᏭ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎤᎾᏖ ᎮᏂ ᏳᎮᏂ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏅᏟᎶᎯᎲᎾ ᏥᎦ ᏂᎯ ᎮᏂ ᏅᏂᏏ ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎯᎸᏍᏄᏒ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᎤᎾᏖ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ jerry ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏪᏥ ᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏣᏥᎨᏳᏛᏅ ᎮᏅ Ꮎ ᎩᎦᎨ ᎠᎾᏗᏔᏍᎬ ᎤᏖᎸᏗᏍᏗ. ᏧᏁᏟᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏤᎸᎯ ᏥᎨᎸ ᎤᎾ. ᏛᏲ ᏱᎦᎭᏖᎳᏓ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏣᎪᎮᎸ ᏱᏕᎯᎳᏬᏥᏕ ᏣᏚᎵᎲ ᏱᎦ ᏢᏲ ᏱᎦᎲᏖᎸᏗ ᏣᎪᎮᎸ ᏧᏅᎪᏨ ᎪᎯᏓ ᏧᏅᎪᏨ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ. ᏁᎲᎾ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏥᏗᎠᎢᏒ ᏧᏬᏢᎯᏌᏅ bull Ꮓ, ᎠᏎᎾ ᏧᏚᏓᎴᏨᏅ. ᎭᏯᏩᏘ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏚᏓᎴᏨᏅ Ᏺ ᎠᎮᏂ. ᎠᏲ Ꮲ ᏱᏓᎦᏕᎸᏗ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ. ᏦᎢ Ꮫ ᏯᏂᎠ ᏕᏥᎪᏩᏘ Ꮲ ᏳᏚᎵᏟᏗ ᎤᏂᏴᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᎦᎬᏛᎦ ᎦᏳᎵᏅ ᎠᏂᏯᎠ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ. ᎠᎮᏅ ᎤᏣᏘᎾ ᎨᎵ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏐᎢ Steve Cambell ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩᏅ ᎾᎮᏂ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎤᏁᎳᏛ ᎮᏂ Ꮲ ᎮᏂ ᎡᎯ ᎠᏂᏁᎵ. Steve Cambell Ꮎ minister, licensed minister Ꮎ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏧᎾ, ᏧᏂᎾᎡᎸ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏧᏛᏅᏒ ᏥᏚᎵᏍᎪᏁᎸ four vision. ᏢᏗᏝ ᏥᏄᏛᏛᏅ ᏧᎷᏨᎾ ᏧᏃᎮᏢ ᏚᎵᏍᎪᏁᎸ ᎤᎾ ᎤᏂᏃᏎᎸ ᎤᏂᎾᎡᎸ ᎪᏪᎳ. ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏳᏲᎯᏍᏓᏁᎴ Ꮟ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎦ. ᏏᏅ ᏥᎦ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᏃᏙ. ᏝᏲᏃ ᎡᏍᎦᏂ ᎤᏁᎨᏯᏛᏅ ᎮᏂ Ꮎ holiness church Ꮲ ᏩᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎨ ᏧᎾᏛᏅ, Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏗ ᏱᎦ ᏗᏓᏬᏍᎩ holiness church ᏥᏲᎮᎸ. Ꮭ ᎮᏂ ᎣᎪᏎ ᎨᎲ ᏳᏭᏅ holiness church ᏳᏣᎵᏥᏙᏂ. ᏂᎮᏂ ᏣᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎬ ᏳᏬᎯᏳᏂ ᏂᎯ ᎮᏂ Baptist ᎮᏂ ᎤᏪᏅᏍᏗ. ᏢᎮᏂ holiness ᏳᎦᎶᎯ
segments.transliteration: asenayo osda henv ogeyosv. naheni salemi tsaneha aya heni tlv gusda otsotlagi yiga yanvda gadusa otse. asena naheni gowela nidodigvnv sgiheni dotsisdawadi. na tlvheni dinadayone yigvniyvha. aya e sawu asena unate heni yuheni gusda nvtlilohihvna tsiga nihi heni nvnisi tsitsiyohehv hilvsnusv. asena unate heni sgina ageyutsa sgiheni jerry tsigehv uwetsi gehv gohiga tsatsigeyudvnv henv na gigage anaditasgv utelvdisdi. tsunetlidi heni utselvhi tsigelv una. dvyo yigahatelada ahani tsagohelv yidehilawotside tsadulihv yiga tlvyo yigahvtelvdi tsagohelv tsunvgotsv gohida tsunvgotsv tsunilawisdi. nehvna tsinulisdvnv tsidiaisv tsuwotlvhisanv bull no, asena tsududaletsvnv. hayawati yusda dudaletsvnv yo aheni. ayo tlv yidagadelvdi tsiyohelv sgina yusdi dunilvwisdanehv. tsoi dv yania detsigowati tlv yudulitlidi uniyvsdi asena tlv gusda yigagvdvga gayulinv aniyaa tsiyohelv. ahenv utsatina geli gehv na soi Steve Cambell hesdi heni osda yiga sgina. usdayvhvsginv naheni usdayvhvsgi uneladv heni tlv heni ehi anineli. Steve Cambell na minister, licensed minister na gowela tsuna, tsuninaelv heni sgina gohiga tsudvnvsv tsidulisgonelv four vision. tlvditla tsinudvdvnv tsulutsvna tsunohetlv dulisgonelv una uninoselv uninaelv gowela. asena tla gusda yuyohisdanele si alitsidohvsga. sinv tsiga alitsidonodo. tlayono esgani unegeyadvnv heni na holiness church tlv walitsidohvsge tsunadvnv, tlv gusda tsulvwisdadi yiga didawosgi holiness church tsiyohelv. tla heni ogose gehv yuwunv holiness church yutsalitsidoni. niheni tsalitsidohvsgv yuwohiyuni nihi heni Baptist heni uwenvsdi. tlvheni holiness yugalohi
segments.translation: Yeah, he had taught us good. Those people around Salem will tell us, “You guys on the mountain don’t understand nothing,” but we were following the word that was in the Bible, because adulterers can’t get in there. There’s one in there, but he knows, I told him, “You might be the reason good things aren’t happening.” But that girl knows. It was Jerry’s daughter. She tried to take part in the communion, and she was acting like a Christian, but they wouldn’t let her. They told her. “You can come to church here as much as you want, but you can’t take part in the communion.” And she got mad and left for a long time. She was out of church for a long time, but when Jerry passed, she came back and rededicated. But Bull, something happened. I’m not quite sure what happened, I told Bull I wasn’t going to take part in that kind of work. There’s about three of them that don’t need to be in there, but I can’t do anything about it. But one was from another place, Steve Campbell. He’s no good. His wife used to be married. Her husband is still alive somewhere, and that’s no good. Steve Campbell is a licensed minister, and they did take it away. He was at Four Vision's [Baptist] Church, and he left for a long time, and when he came back, he told them he lied to them. He said they had taken his license away but that didn’t stop him from going around and preaching, and even today he still preaches, but not around here. They don’t let him around here, they said he was preaching at some Holiness church. “A Baptist ain’t got no business at a Holiness church,” I told him. That’s what they used to tell us. If a Baptist was preaching at a Holiness church and if that person believes, he will have to go to a Baptist church, not a Holiness church.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᏛᏙ ᏄᏅᏂ
segments.transliteration: sgi dvdo nunvni
segments.translation: That’s the way they have it.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎣᎨᏲᎾ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sgi heni nusdv ogeyona aya gehv
segments.translation: That’s how we are taught.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏣᏗᎲ ᎪᎯ ᏥᏣᎴᏅᎲ ᏕᎭᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᎢᎦᏛ ᏨᏂᏍᏓᏂᏙᎴ ᏙᎭ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: tsadihv gohi tsitsalenvhv dehadelaquasgv igadv tsvnisdanidole doha tsalagiha hiwonisga tsigehv
segments.translation: You said a while ago, when you started school, you had a rough time because you only spoke Cherokee.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᏆᎥ ᏗᏩᎵᏍᏗ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᎮᏂ ᏂᏗᎬᏩᏓᎴᏅᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᎠᎮᏅ ᎤᏢᏂᎩᏗ ᎤᏁᎳᏅ, ᎤᏁᏟᏴᏒ. ᎡᏅᏨᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏅᏃ ᏥᏥᎣᏓᏩᏗᏒ ᎦᏗᏔᏍᎬ. ᎡᏧᎵᎭᏭᏛ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎭᎴᏫᏍᏓ ᏴᏬᏎᎳ. ᏅᏃ ᎠᏰᏟ ᎠᏩᎴᏫᏍᏛᏅ. ᎠᏩᏠᏒ ᏗᎩᎶᏒ ᏗᏝ ᏩᎩᎶᏒ. ᎩᏗᏬᏠ ᏫᏗᏥᎦᏃ car ᏗᏝ ᏩᎲ. ᎩᎶ ᎡᏲ ᎠᏩᏝᏃᎮᏙ ᎠᏩᏛ ᏅᏍᎫ ᎠᎩᏴᏍᏕᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎮᏅ ᎲᏅ ᏯᏩᏘ ᏱᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᏭ. ᏧᏫᎭᏂᎦ Ꮲ ᏫᎲᎦ Ꮎ ᏥᏣᏦᏓ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ, ᏙᎯᎳᏫᏤᏒᎢ. ᎫᏍᏓ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎠᏩᏟᏃᎮᏛ ᏩᏩᏣᏅ car Ꭲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏲᏍᎫ ᎤᎾᏭ ᎠᏬᏢ ᏌᎾᎴ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ. ᏌᎾᎴ ᎠᎦᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎩᎶ ᎠᏩᏢᏃᎮᏛ ᎠᏮᏏ ᏅᎨᎲ ᎦᏛᎩᏍᎬ ᎡᏲ ᎬᏬᏂᎲ ᏞᏲ ᎩᎶ ᏱᏥᎪᏩᏘᎮ. ᎾᎯᏳ Ꭱ ᎠᏩᏓᏁᏟᏴᏒ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏩᎩᎶᏒ. ᏝᏃ ᎸᎯᏳ ᏝᏃ ᏱᎦᎨᎾ, ᎠᏯ ᏗᎩᎶᏒ. ᎯᏗᏝ ᎠᎦᏓ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ Ꮟ ᏔᎵ ᏍᎪ ᏔᎵᏍᎪᎯ ᏣᏁᎵ ᏛᎮᏃ ᎾᏕᏘᏱ Ꮓ
segments.transliteration: nahiyu heni awadelaquav diwalisdi, nahiyu heni nidigvwadalenvdi sgina. ahenv utlvnigidi unelanv, unetliyvsv. envtsvnv sgu nvno tsitsiodawadisv gaditasgv. etsulihawudv ahani halewisda yvwosela. nvno ayetli awalewisdvnv. awatlosv digilosv ditla wagilosv. gidiwotlo widitsigano car ditla wahv. gilo eyo awatlanohedo awadv nvsgu agiyvsdeda gehv ahenv hvnv yawati yinawalisdanewu. tsuwihaniga tlv wihvga na tsitsatsoda awohelv, dohilawitsesvi. gusda sgi yusda awatlinohedv wawatsanv car i asena yosgu unawu awotlv sanale igohida. sanale agasgasdanelv heni gilo awatlvnohedv awvsi nvgehv gadvgisgv eyo gvwonihv tleyo gilo yitsigowatihe. nahiyu e awadanetliyvsv tsunilawisdi wagilosv. tlano lvhiyu tlano yigagena, aya digilosv. hiditla agada gatsiyohelv si tali sgo talisgohi tsaneli dvheno nadetiyi no
segments.translation: It was hard because we all went through that. I was always mad because I didn’t understand and did not know why all the other kids had mothers and I didn’t have one and it made me mad. I didn’t understand why. I was always mad at someone and that’s why I learned how to fight. From that time on I found out how strong God is. One time I was somewhere far away driving and drinking, and I was told to stop, and I stopped in the middle of the road, and I go out and walked back and sat down and looked toward my car. Someone was talking to me, but I knew I was drunk, and I didn’t know what was happening to me. Something had told me to park that car somewhere go home and go to church. Something was talking to me like that. I got back in my car and just sat there until morning. That scared me because someone was talking to me, and I was by myself. I could hear someone talking but I couldn’t see anybody. I changed then and started going to church. I never will go back to where I was at. I’m going forward. It’s been 28 years.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮓ ᎾᏕᏘᏱ ᏗᏣᎶᏒ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎭᎴᏂᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: no nadetiyi ditsalosv yusdi halenidohv
segments.translation: It’s been 28 years since you’ve calmed down being the way that you were.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏗᏃ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᏯᏩᏚᎸᎮ, ᎠᏂᏧᏤ ᎠᏂᎷᎦ Ᏺ ᎪᎯᏓ ᏧᎶᏒ ᎣᏂ ᎨᎲ ᏥᏕᎾ, ᏥᏕᎾ Ꮟ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ. ᏍᎫᏛ ᏱᎾᎩᏥᏏ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᏩᏨᏏ ᏢᎮᏂ ᏯᏬᎯᏳ ᎠᎩᎷᎯᏍᏗ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ. ᏞᏍᏗ ᏯᏪᏂ Ꮲ ᏭᏂᎶᏒ ᎣᎾ ᎸᏢ ᏂᎦᏥᏪᏎᎸ, ᏢᏛ ᏓᏂᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᏧᏂ ᏣᏁᏙᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᎤᏂᎪᏗ ᎮᏂᏲ ᎤᎾᏓᏁᏟᏴᏒ Ꮩ ᏄᎾᏛᏁᎸ. ᎤᏂᎪᏗᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏙᎩᏲᎱᏌ Ꮎ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏣᏃᎦᏍᏛᏅᏍᎩ. ᎠᏅᏛᏁᎵᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏫᏙᎩᏲᎱᏌ. Ꮭ ᏯᏁ
segments.transliteration: dino alvhiyu yawadulvhe, anitsutse aniluga yo gohida tsulosv oni gehv tsidena, tsidena si sawu yuwagada. sgudv yinagitsisi sawu yuwawatsvsi tlvheni yawohiyu agiluhisdi gatsiyohehv. tlesdi yaweni tlv wunilosv ona lvtlv nigatsiweselv, tlvdv daninigisgv tsuni tsanedohv sgina. unigodi heniyo unadanetliyvsv do nunadvnelv. unigodinv sgu dogiyohusa na gusda tsanogasdvnvsgi. anvdvnelihv sgina widogiyohusa. tla yane
segments.translation: But the boys used to come around and say, “Let’s go back, let’s go back one more time.” That’s all it would take for me, just one time. I would never come back. I didn’t go back, and they went away. And it was later, they were having a singing somewhere and they were there. But a lot of them had changed. All of them settled down, but we lost a lot of them to smoking that stuff. They were doing a lot of stuff and they’re no longer alive.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏁ Ꮓ ᎯᏃ ᏯᏛᎾ ᎦᏥᏯᏛᏛᎲᏍᎬ Ꭰ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᏳᏛᏂ ᎩᎶ. ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏩᏅᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᏳᏛᏂ ᎩᎶ ᎾᎨ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᎪᎯ ᏥᏃᎮᏢᏍᎪ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏙᏗᎦᏛᏒ ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ, ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏙ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎨᏒ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᏕᏗ ᎨᏒ ᎢᏓᎴᏂᏙᎲ ᏥᏕᏛᎵᏍᏕᎵᏍᎬ ᎢᎦᏓ. ᏃᎴᏅ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏢᎦ ᏃᎴ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏝ ᏧᏩᏂᏍᏕᎵᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎩᎶ Ꮄ ᏁᎲᎾ ᏱᎦ ᏃᎴ ᎦᏚᎦ ᏧᏂᏍᏆᎸᎡᎰ. ᏍᎩᎨᏴ ᏪᏙᎰ ᎭᏓᏅᏖᏢᏍᎬ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ
segments.transliteration: tla yane no hino yadvna gatsiyadvdvhvsgv a atsalagi yudvni gilo. dohv usdi wanvdisgo atsalagi yudvni gilo nage etiyv tsinusdidanv gohi tsinohetlvsgo nusdv dodigadvsv iditsalagi, iditsalagi udo atsalagi gesv nusdv udedi gesv idalenidohv tsidedvlisdelisgv igada. nolenv gilo yutlvga nole una ditla tsuwanisdelisgo nole gilo le nehvna yiga nole gaduga tsunisqualveho. sgigeyv wedoho hadanvtetlvsgv atsalagi
segments.translation: They’re not alive now. Say for instance if someone says, “Cherokee,” what do you think of? Was it like how we grew up a long time ago? The way a Cherokee ought to be, and ought to live? The way we used to help if someone got sick? Or if someone passed, they would get together? Is that how far back you think?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏓ ᏛᏲᏃ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏓ, ᏢᎮᏂ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏃ ᏧᎾᎵᏍᏕᎸᎯ ᏱᎦ ᎤᎾᏗᎦᎴᏲᏥ ᎮᏂ ᏴᏫ. ᏥᎪᏩᏘᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ. ᎪᎯᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎩᎶ ᏱᏧᏢᎦ ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏁᎬ ᎠᏂᏍᏕᎸᎮᎬ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎠᏂᏅᎬᎵᏍᎬ, ᎠᎾᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ ᏃᎴ Ꮎ ᎠᎹ ᏱᎦ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏂᏅᎬᎵᏍᎬ. ᎠᏓ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏓᏂᏍᏆᎵᏍᎬ ᏲᎮᏂ ᎠᏮᏖᎸᏛ ᏍᎩ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎵᎲ ᎠᎸᎯᏳᏅ ᎯᎸᏍᎬ ᏧᏒᎯᏓ ᏲᏤᏓ ᎨᎲ. ᏃᎴ Ꮓ ᎣᏏᏭ ᏯᏟᎩᎳ ᏦᏨᏗᎦᎴᏲᎬ. ᏳᏲᎱᏌᏅ ᎩᎶ ᏍᎫᏅ ᏍᎩ ᎾᏅ ᏛᏁᎲ ᏍᎫ ᎯᎸᏍᎦ ᏧᏒᎯᏓ. ᎠᏂᏍᏆᏂᎪᏗᎲ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎫᏴ ᎣᏥᏍᏓᏩᏕᎬ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏏᏗ Ᏼ. ᏍᎫ ᏛᏴ ᏫᎦᎩᎷᎯᏍᏗ ᏲᎪᏏᏅ ᎨᎲ. ᏍᎫ ᏩᏍᏛ Ꮓ. ᏙᏣᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᏬᏣᏗᎦᎴᏲᎬ, ᎪᎯᏅ ᏥᎦ Ꮭ. ᏍᎫ ᏛᏂᎦ ᏥᏓᏅᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎡᏧᎵᎭᏭ ᏯᎾᎵᎮᎵᎦ ᎤᏂᎩᏌ ᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎰ
segments.transliteration: hesda dvyono sgi yinusda, tlvheni hesdi heno tsunalisdelvhi yiga unadigaleyotsi heni yvwi. tsigowatisgv gehv. gohiga heni tsigehv gilo yitsutlvga una heni anegv anisdelvhegv galitsode aninvgvlisgv, anadasdayvhvsgv nole na ama yiga gusda aninvgvlisgv. ada leyiga danisqualisgv yoheni awvtelvdv sgi nanadvnelihv alvhiyunv hilvsgv tsusvhida yotseda gehv. nole no osiwu yatligila tsotsvdigaleyogv. yuyohusanv gilo sgunv sgi nanv dvnehv sgu hilvsga tsusvhida. anisquanigodihv igohida. sgina sguyv otsisdawadegv tsunadanisidi yv. sgu dvyv wigagiluhisdi yogosinv gehv. sgu wasdv no. dotsanigisgv wotsadigaleyogv, gohinv tsiga tla. sgu dvniga tsidanvlisdayvhvsgi etsulihawu yanaliheliga unigisa nawalisdaneho
segments.translation: It’s not like that anymore. People have scattered away, as far as I can see. Long time ago when someone was sick, that’s where everyone would go and help. They would clean and cook. They would finish cleaning and go cut wood. I would join in on things like that. Sometimes we were there for a few days and then when they got better, we would just scatter away. When someone would pass away, that’s what they would do, too. They would stay a few days until they would bury him. We would follow them all the way to the grave and they would say, “This is as far as we can go.” Then we all scatter away but nowadays they just get together and eat like they’re happy they left.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎦᏚᏌ ᏥᏤᎲ, ᏍᎩᎨ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎳ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏕᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᎮ ᎾᎠ ᏗᏣᏓᎵ
segments.transliteration: nana tsadihv gadusa tsitsehv, sgige yinulisdanidola nigada detsalisdelihe naa ditsadali
segments.translation: Like you said earlier, did you all up the hill help each other when that would happen?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᎩᎶ ᏛᏍᎫ ᏱᏧᏍᏓᏲᎯᏎ ᎨᎲ ᏂᎦᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏤᎬ ᎣᏥᏍᏕᎸᎮᎬ ᏱᏧᏢᎩ ᏱᎦ ᏳᏄᎸᎲᏍᎩᏅ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᏱᎦ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎤᎩᏍᏗ. ᏂᎦᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎣᏤᎬ ᏗᎨᏛᏍᏗ ᏙᏥᏍᏆᎵᏍᎬ ᏗᏗᏍᏓ ᏓᏃᏢᏍᎬ. ᏌᏭᏅ ᏴᏫ ᎡᎲ truck ᎤᎯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏬᏥᏯᏂᏍᎬ ᏩᏂᏴᏂᏍᎬ ᎴᏱᎦ nick Springwater ᏚᏙᎥ ᎤᏔᏂ truck ᏧᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᎷᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏫᏛᎲᏍᎬ. Ꮓ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎠᏂᎩᏍᏗᎲ Ꮂ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏠᏯᏍᏕᎮ ᏙᎮᏂ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎤᏱᎦ ᎠᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏍᏗᎦᎭ ᎠᎾᏗᎦᎴᏴᏍᎬ ᎾᏅ ᎤᏢᎩ ᏍᏓᏯ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏓᏁᎰ ᏍᎨᏲ ᎤᎪᏓ ᏩᏂᏁᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏙᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᏄᎾ ᏕᎦᏛ ᏢᎮᏂ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏍᎪᎯᏍᏆ ᎤᎾᏓᎨᏓ ᏓᏂᏁᎲ, ᏚᏯᏅ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎾᏭ ᎮᏂ sack ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᏓᏂᎾᏗᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏢᏅ plastic ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᎨᎮ. ᏩᏂᏁᎲ ᎢᏌ ᏅᏱᎦ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ. Ꮂ ᏯᏩᏖ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ bolonia ᎾᎯᏳ
segments.transliteration: v, gilo dvsgu yitsusdayohise gehv nigadi heni otsegv otsisdelvhegv yitsutlvgi yiga yunulvhvsginv alisdadi yiga gusda ugisdi. nigadi heni inage otsegv digedvsdi dotsisqualisgv didisda danotlvsgv. sawunv yvwi ehv truck uhi sgina wotsiyanisgv waniyvnisgv leyiga nick Springwater dudov utani truck tsuhv. sgina galugv sgina awidvhvsgv. no alisdadi anigisdihv hv gusda gilo yutloyasdehe doheni alisdadi uyiga anigisgv nowunv sdigaha anadigaleyvsgv nanv utlvgi sdaya tsinulisdaneho sgeyo ugoda wanineho tsigehv. doheni na nuna degadv tlvheni gusda yigehe sgohisqua unadageda daninehv, duyanv asena nawu heni sack nahiyu tsidaninadihv nahiyu tsigehv tlvnv plastic gusda yigehe. waninehv isa nvyiga tsudalenvdi sgi yusda. hv yawate yusdi gehv bolonia nahiyu
segments.translation: Even if someone was having a hard time we would go and help them out. Or if they were sick or if he needed to buy something to eat, we would all go to the woods and cut posts and make railroad ties. There was one person who had a truck, and they would go get him. His name was Nick Springwater. He had a big truck. He would come and take those, and they would buy food with it. We never got any of that. They would give some of that out especially to the one who was sick. 100 lbs. sack of potatoes wasn’t nothing and they would also give them a bag of beans. They would just put them in plastic bags. Or that would give them flour and things like that. I didn’t know what bologna was back then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏌ ᏤᎲ ᏏᏅᏗ ᏳᏓᎳ bolonia ᏦᏥᎩᏍᎪ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏗᏎᎯᏍᏗ ᏳᏁᏌ bolonia ᏧᏩᎩᏍᎬ Ꮓ ᏥᏛᏲᎩᏴᏂᏍᎬ Ꭷ ᏗᏣᎵᏍᏓᏄᎦ. ᎥᎩᏙ Ꮫ ᏤᎲ ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏙᏍᏛᎵᏟᏐ bolonia ᎣᎩᏂᏯᎴᎬ. ᏃᎴ Ꮕ ᏥᎾᏗᎲ ᎩᎶ ᏁᎲᎾ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᎾ ᎾᎯᏳ Ꮕ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎤᏅᏏᏭ ᏣᏂᏍᎪᏍᎬ ᎦᏙ ᏙᎭ ᎤᏂᏂᏐᏗ ᎤᎵᏨᏙᏩᏗ ᏣᏂᎯᎵᏙᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ. ᏌᎾᎴ Ꮓ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎤᏂᏍᎪᏐᏅ ᏥᎨᏐ
segments.transliteration: elisa tsehv sinvdi yudala bolonia tsotsigisgo adela disehisdi yunesa bolonia tsuwagisgv no tsidvyogiyvnisgv ka ditsalisdanuga. vgido dv tsehv sgasdi dosdvlitliso bolonia oginiyalegv. nole nv tsinadihv gilo nehvna yinulisdvna nahiyu nv tsigesv unvsiwu tsanisgosgv gado doha uninisodi ulitsvdowadi tsanihilidoho yudaha. sanale no gayula unisgosonv tsigeso
segments.translation: When my grandma was alive, we would eat bologna once a month when she got her check. She would buy bologna and call us. Me and my sister would take off running. Like we said a while ago, they would hand dig that grave, and they would dig all night. In the morning, they already have it dug.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏍᎩ n ᏍᎫ ᏧᎨᎲ ᏞᏍᏗ ᎤᎵᏧᏚᏩᏗ ᏱᏧᏢᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎦ ᏧᎨᎲ. ᎮᏍᏗ ᎤᏁᎸᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏕᏍᏗ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎬᏗ ᏣᏄᏢᏍᎬ ᏳᏂᏍᎪᏐᏂ ᎤᎩᏨᏗ ᏴᎩᎳ Ꮓ ᏣᏄᏞᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎮᏂ ᏧᎦᎴᏙ ᏦᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᏧᏃᏢ. Ꮭ ᎮᏂ Ᏺ ᏅᏱ ᏱᏘᏩᏛ ᎤᎾ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎤᎾ ᏙᎩᏍᎪᏒ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᏚᏂᏲᎱᏎᎸ. ᎤᎾ ᏦᎩᏍᎪᏒ ᏗᎪᏕᏍᏗᏭ ᎬᏗ. ᏦᏥᎪᏩᏘᏍᎬ ᏐᎢ ᎦᏂᏌᎲ ᎯᎤᏭ ᎮᏂ ᏂᏚᏓᎵ ᏕᎦᏂᏌ ᏴᏫ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏂᎧᎵ ᎮᏂ. ᏏᏭᏅ ᎠᏂᏩᏘᎰ Ꮲ ᏙᏥᎪᏩᏘᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᏐᎢ ᎦᏂᏌᎲ ᎠᎭᏂᏅ ᏗᏝ ᎤᎾᏅ ᎠᏰᏟ ᏦᎩᏍᎪᏒ. ᎾᏅ ᏕᎦᏒᏙᏍᎬ ᎠᎹ ᏣᏂᏍᏚᏟᎲ ᏓᏂᏅᏘᎲ ᎦᏓ. ᎡᎵᏭ box Ꭲ ᏭᎳᏗᏍᏗ ᏍᎫᏭᏅ ᏂᏚᏓᎸ ᏕᎦᏂᏌᎲ. Ꮂ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏂᎬ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏓ ᎤᎾ ᎡᏲ ᏥᏙᏥᏍᎪᏍᎬ Ᏺ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ. ᏔᎵ ᏙᎩᏍᎪᏒ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᏚᏂᏂᏌᏅ salem ᎢᎾ Ꮓ ᎢᎢ ᏅᏲ ᏛᏲ ᎤᎾ. ᎪᎯᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᏔᏍᎩᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏓᏅᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sgi n sgu tsugehv tlesdi ulitsuduwadi yitsutlvsgesdi anadisga tsugehv. hesdi unelvgi yinusdesdi gusda gvdi tsanutlvsgv yunisgosoni ugitsvdi yvgila no tsanutlesgv na heni tsugaledo tsonadanisodi tsunotlv. tla heni yo nvyi yitiwadv una tsunadanisodi una dogisgosv tsunasdi dv duniyohuselv. una tsogisgosv digodesdiwu gvdi. tsotsigowatisgv soi ganisahv hiuwu heni nidudali deganisa yvwi una anikali heni. siwunv aniwatiho tlv dotsigowatisgv na soi ganisahv ahaninv ditla unanv ayetli tsogisgosv. nanv degasvdosgv ama tsanisdutlihv daninvtihv gada. eliwu box i wuladisdi sguwunv nidudalv deganisahv. hv yawanvti nigv sgi yinusda una eyo tsidotsisgosgv yo sgi tsinusdv. tali dogisgosv unana tsunasdi duninisanv salem ina no ii nvyo dvyo una. gohige tsigehv ditasgisdi heni yidanvdi tsigehv
segments.translation: That too. They would say, “Don’t leave it uncovered all night.” Back then, if they got done digging the grave, they would say, “Don’t leave it uncovered.” and cover it up and then uncover it in the morning. That Chuculate Cemetery, you’re not going to find any rocks there. They lost some little ones. That place is full. They would still find a space and there would be a grave on each side, and they would pour water on the side to keep the dirt from falling and that box to go in there. I don’t know if it was like that everywhere, but where we dug it was like that. We dug two graves there where we buried two little ones. At Salem, it’s rocky and a long time ago they used to use dynamite.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᏙᏛ ᏅᏲ ᏱᎦ Ꮓ ᏗᏔᏍᎩᏍᏓ ᏓᏅᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: yeah, dodv nvyo yiga no ditasgisda danvdihv
segments.translation: Yeah, really. When it was rocky, they’d use Dynamite.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏅᏱ ᏓᏂᏲᏍᏗᎲ ᏗᏔᏍᎩᏍᏓ ᏱᏓᏅᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏛᏲ ᎾᎠ ᏳᏥᎷᎨ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎾᏛᎾᏛᏁᎵ ᎦᏚ ᎡᏗᏝ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎦᏍᎪᏍᎬ ᎦᏙ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏅᏱ ᏳᏬᎬᏂᎳ ᏅᏃ ᏗᏝ ᏬᎦᏕᎵᎬ. ᏧᎾᏛᎾ ᎤᎾᏓ ᎾᏅᏛᏁᎲ ᏫᏓᎾᏔᏍᎩᏍᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: na nvyi daniyosdihv ditasgisda yidanvdi tsigehv. dvyo naa yutsiluge sgi yinadvnadvneli gadu editla gehv osda heni tsigasgosgv gado gehv na nvyi yuwogvnila nvno ditla wogadeligv. tsunadvna unada nanvdvnehv widanatasgisdihv
segments.translation: They would use dynamite. I didn’t get close when they would do that. I would dig on top for a little until I hit a rock and then they would use dynamite and we would dive down the road. Adults who knew what they were doing was blowing it Up.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏝᎨᏲ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎰᏪᎵᏍᎦ ᏱᎦ ᎯᎪᎵᏰᏍᎦ?
segments.transliteration: tlageyo atsalagi howelisga yiga higoliyesga?
segments.translation: Can you read and write Cherokee?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, ᏗᏥᎪᎵᏰᏍᎨ ᏳᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮎ ᎩᏔᏯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲᏭ Ꮫ ᏂᏕᏣᏓᏛᏁᎴ ᏕᏣᎩᎡᎴ ᏣᏬᏎᎸ ᎠᏎᎮ. ᏣᎩᏑᎵᎪᏨᏭᎮᏂ ᏕᏥᎳᏫᏥᏙᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎠᎩᏍᏗᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏕᏥᎪᎵᏰᏍᎬ ᏗᏣᎳᎩ. ᏲᎮᏂ salemᎢ ᏗᏣᎳᎩ ᏗᏂᎪᎵᏰᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᎦ. ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏓᏩᏕᎳᏆᎥ. ᏢᏴ ᏧᏩᏮᏛᏏᏌᏅ Ꮲ ᏧᏩᎩᎶᏒ Ꮓ ᏫᏓᏮᎨᏫᏒ ᏗᏣᎳᎩ. ᏓᎩᏁ ᎠᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎪᏛ ᏗᏩᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: hvv, ditsigoliyesge yulisdvnv asena na gitaya tsigehv nigalisdihvwu dv nidetsadadvnele detsagiele tsawoselv asehe. tsagisuligotsvwuheni detsilawitsidohv asena agisdiwu tsigehv detsigoliyesgv ditsalagi. yoheni salemi ditsalagi dinigoliyesgi tsigehv gohiga. una heni dawadelaquav. tlvyv tsuwawvdvsisanv tlv tsuwagilosv no widawvgewisv ditsalagi. dagine aheni aginulvhvsgodv diwadelaquasdi
segments.translation: I used to, but Jerry told me, “You misused it,” and got it taken away. That was about when I stopped going to church, but I was little when I started reading Cherokee. They used to read Cherokee at Salem long time ago and that’s where I learned some. When I grew up and went away and I forgot it. I have a few books, but I can’t read Them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎲ yeah, ᎯᎾ ᏥᏂᏛᏛᏁ Cherokee nation ᏣᏢᏂᎬᏁ ᎢᎩᏲᎱᏎᏗ ᏂᎨᏒᏅ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎢᏗᏬᏂᏍᎦ ᎨᏒ Ꮩ ᎮᎵᏍᎪ ᏂᎯ?
segments.transliteration: vhv yeah, hina tsinidvdvne Cherokee nation tsatlvnigvne igiyohusedi nigesvnv tsalagi idiwonisga gesv do helisgo nihi?
segments.translation: What do you think about what CN is doing and the effort to not lose the language?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᏛᏂᎩᏐᏂ ᏍᎩᎾᏅ ᏓᏁᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ. ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᎮᎾ ᏥᏈᏍᏓ ᎠᏁ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏯᏂᎪᎵ, ᏯᏂᏬᏂ, ᏯᏃᏪᎸᎩᏅ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ Ꮩ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎦᎵᏍᏙᏗ ᎮᎲ Ꮲ. Ꮭ ᏓᎩᏲᎱᏎᎵ, ᏏᏭ ᎮᏅ ᎤᏁᎳᎩᏅ ᏓᎩᏲᎱᏎᎳ ᏣᎾᏗ, ᏏᏭᎭᎮᏂ ᏓᎩᏲᎱᏎᎵ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᎮᎾ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏛᏂᎩᏏᏂ. ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᎠᏎᎾ, ᎾᎮᏂ jehova ᎬᎩᏩᏛᎯᏙᎰ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎰ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏱᎬᏩᏠᏃᎮᏗ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎦᏥᎦᏎᏍᏙ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏱᎦ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎮᏂ Ꮟ ᎾᏂᏪ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎲ ᏏᏅ ᎯᎢ ᏥᏗᏬᏂ ᎨᎲ. ᏍᏗᎩᏛ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏭᏍᎫ ᎬᏩᎴᏅᏗ ᎠᏩᎦᏎᏍᏙ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎾᏅᏛᏁᎲ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏛᏅᏍᎬᏂ. ᎯᎮᏂ ᏥᎦ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᏙᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᎾᎵᏒᎲᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏄᎾᏓᎴ ᎮᏂ ᎤᎬᏫᏳ Ꮓ ᎠᎾᎢ. ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏯ ᏂᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏛᏂᎩᏐᏂ
segments.transliteration: nadv aniyonega dvnigisoni sginanv daneyohvsgi atsalagi. aniyonega hena tsiquisda ane tsalagiha yanigoli, yaniwoni, yanowelvginv aya heni do sgi yigalisdodi hehv tlv. tla dagiyohuseli, siwu henv unelaginv dagiyohusela tsanadi, siwuhaheni dagiyohuseli heni aniyonega hena sgina dvnigisini. gelisgo aya gehv tla yawanvti asena, naheni jehova gvgiwadvhidoho aniyonega heni geho atsalagiha yigvwatlonohedi. asena osda gatsigasesdo hesdi heni utloyi yiga nudale heni si naniwe aniwonihv sinv hii tsidiwoni gehv. sdigidv gohiga wusgu gvwalenvdi awagasesdo gusda nanvdvnehv nigalisdvnvsgvni. hiheni tsiga anitsalagi doheni gehv anitsalagi analisvhvsgi heni nunadale heni ugvwiyu no anai. sgi heni aya nigelisgv aniyonega heni dvnigisoni
segments.translation: The white people are getting it all and they’re teaching Cherokee. There’s a lot of white people who can talk it, read it, and write it. That’s the way we should be. That ought to be us that are like that, because we’re going to lose it again and the white people are going to take it over. That’s what I think. The Jehovah’s come and see me and they’re all talking Cherokee. And I listen well, but they don’t say the words right. They say it different than the way we’re talking here. I been watching out for a long time about how things are happening. The real Cherokees that exist now they’re going to pass on. The Whites are going to get it all.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏢᏴ ᏫᏛᎵᏒᏂ ᎮᎵᏍᎪ, Ꮩ ᎧᎵᎢ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎨᏒ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: tlvyv widvlisvni helisgo, do kalii atsalagi gesv gawonihisdi
segments.translation: So, you think Cherokee language is going to fade away some day?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎯᏛᏅ ᎣᏂ ᏥᏚᎾᏛᏏᏓ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᎰ ᎬᎩᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎲ ᏗᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎦᏥᎵᏃᎮᏙ ᎠᏃᏟᎩ ᎮᏂᏲ ᎠᎮᏅ ᏢᏍᎩᏂ ᏱᎬᏂᏁᎦ Ᏺ ᏢᏲ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏯᏃᏟᎩ ᎠᏎᎾ. ᏱᏥᎾᎸᏍᏛᏂ ᎮᏂ Ᏺ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏱᎮᏅ ᏱᏓᎦᏫᏂ ᏱᏓᎧᏁᎦ ᎮᏅ Ᏺ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏎᎾ. ᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᏎ ᎬᎾᎸᏍᏙᏗ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏣᏛᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏭᎮᏂ ᏣᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏥᏲᏎᎰ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᎤᏟᎪᏭ ᎮᏂ Ᏺ ᏳᏪᏍᏗ ᏳᎵᏍᎦᎮᏛᏂ. ᏔᎵᎭᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏧᏒᎯᏓ ᏯᎩᏁᎵ ᎠᏭᏅ ᏂᎬᏗ
segments.transliteration: hidvnv oni tsidunadvsida igada tsunasdi nigeho gvgisdawadidohv ditsalagiha gatsilinohedo anotligi heniyo ahenv tlvsgini yigvninega yo tlvyo nigada yanotligi asena. yitsinalvsdvni heni yo na usdi ageyutsa yihenv yidagawini yidakanega henv yo tsalagi asena. hesdi ase gvnalvsdodi yiga sgi yitsadvdi osda wuheni tsawonihisdi tsiyoseho. asena utligowu heni yo yuwesdi yulisgahedvni. talihanv sgu tsusvhida yagineli awunv nigvdi
segments.translation: This next generation, some of these kids follow me around. I talk to them in Cherokee, and they understand, but they don’t speak. But if I make that little girl mad, she’ll talk Cherokee a little bit. She’ll say a word in Cherokee and then I tell her, “I shouldn’t have to make you mad to speak Cherokee; you should just be able to do it.” She doesn’t even know what to say when she gets mad, but she’ll be mad for two days. And she’s just this [gestures] tall.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎭᎳᎩ ᎾᏂ ᏗᏣᏓᎵᏌ?
segments.transliteration: halagi nani ditsadalisa?
segments.translation: How many grandkids do you have?

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᏞᏍᏛ ᎠᏮᏏ ᎨᎲ ᏗᏩᏓᎵᏏ ᎨᎲ ᏰᏁᎭ, ᏓᏩᏓᏚᏥᏴ Ꭱ GᏈᏍᏙᏒ ᎠᏁ ᏌᏭ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏧᏣ Ꮲ ᎡᎯ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᏥᎪᎥ. ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᏁᎳᏓ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎥᏩᎵᏍᏚᏛᏅ. ᎥᎩᎶᎠᏍᏛᏅ ᏙᎨ ᏴᏓ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᎪᏁᎸ ᏲᏁᎦ. ᏛᏍᎫ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎾᎮᏂ blackfoot ᏥᏓᏃᎮ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᎪᏁᎸ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎤᏓᏘᎾ, ᎩᎾᏓᏘᎾᎡᏍᏗ ᎠᏬᏎᎸ Ꮥ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎤᎾᏓᏒᎸᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏧᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎠᏎ ᏦᎩᎾᏨᏍᏙᏗ ᏃᎩᏅᏁᎸ. ᏗᎩᎾᏨᏍᏛ ᎤᏲᎱᏎᎸ, ᏭᏲᎱᏎᎸ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ Ꮂ ᏯᏩmᏘ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏎ ᏱᏄᏕᎳ ᏍᎩᏅ ᎠᏯ ᎠᏩᏤᎳ ᎤᏛᏅ. ᏢᏴ ᏫᏙᎩᎾᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎣᏂ ᏏᏩ ᏃᎴ ᏫᏙᎩᎾᏙᎵᏨ ᏃᏲᏙ ᏭᏓᏘᏅᏁ ᏲᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎦᎵᏅ ᏔᎵᏁ ᏫᏙᎩᎾᎦᎴᏅᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꮓ. Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ Ᏺ ᏩᏛ Ᏺ ᎸᏢ ᎠᎮᎾ ᏢᎮᏂ Ᏼ ᏥᏂᎦᏛ ᎦᏥᎪᎥ, ᎲᏃ ᎸᎯᏳ ᎤᏛᏁ ᏲᏃ ᏅᎩ ᏍᎪᎯ ᎮᏅ Ꮲ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ Ꮲ ᎡᎯ ᎠᏎ ᎠᏧᏣ. Ꮭ ᏍᎫ ᏱᎬᏩᏚᎳ ᏥᎪᏩᏛᏗ ᎭᎳᏛ ᏳᏁᎩᏟᏓ ᎨᎵᎰ
segments.transliteration: tlesdv awvsi gehv diwadalisi gehv yeneha, dawadadutsiyv e Gquisdosv ane sawu usdi atsutsa tlv ehi asena usdi tsigehv gatsigov. gohiga tsigehv awanelada asena vwalisdudvnv. vgiloasdvnv doge yvda awalisgonelv yonega. dvsgu yonega naheni blackfoot tsidanohe awalisgonelv usdi udatina, ginadatinaesdi awoselv de sdigida unadasvlvdi yusdi tsugayvlige ase tsoginatsvsdodi noginvnelv. diginatsvsdv uyohuselv, wuyohuselv na usdi hv yawamti sgu ase yinudela sginv aya awatsela udvnv. tlvyv widoginalenvhv asena oni siwa nole widoginadolitsv noyodo wudatinvne yodo sgina asena galinv taline widoginagalenvdi gehv no. na atsutsa yo wadv yo lvtlv ahena tlvheni yv tsinigadv gatsigov, hvno lvhiyu udvne yono nvgi sgohi henv tlv yudetiyvda tlv ehi ase atsutsa. tla sgu yigvwadula tsigowadvdi haladv yunegitlida geliho
segments.translation: I don’t have any grandkids, but I have a lot of nieces and nephews. One boy somewhere. I haven’t seen him since he was a baby. I left a long time ago. I got tricked, I got lied to, it was a Blackfoot. She lied to me, and she told me we’re going to have a child. Her parents were kind of high and they made us get married, so we got married. She lost it, she lost the baby. I don’t know if she did it on purpose and one day we separated. We got together again and then one day she did have a child, but we had already separated again, and that boy grew up somewhere. I haven’t seen him since he was this [gestures] tall. He's grown now, he's about 40 years old and he lives somewhere. I wouldn’t want to see him; I wonder how ugly he is.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎬᎵᎡᎵᎦ ᏕᏓᏝᏃᎲᎳ
segments.transliteration: gvlieliga dedatlanohvla
segments.translation: I glad we talked.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎥᎥ, ᎠᏯᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎬᎵᎡᎵᎦ, ᎠᏯ ᏍᎫ ᎬᎵᎡᎵᎦ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎦ ᏕᏓᏝᏃᎲᎳ
segments.transliteration: vv, ayanv sgu gvlieliga, aya sgu gvlieliga sgi tsiga dedatlanohvla
segments.translation: Yeah I'm glad too, im glad too we talked.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ ᏛᎭ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎨᎰ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎯ ᏗᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᎢᎬᏅᏥᏙᎲᏭ ᏂᎦᎥ ᎫᏍᏓ yeah
segments.transliteration: yudaha dvha sdayi geho sgi ihi ditlanohedi igvnvtsidohvwu nigav gusda yeah
segments.translation: Sometimes it's hard to talk that much because we're in a rush with everything, yeah.

segments.speaker: harry-daugherty
segments.text: ᎢᎪᎯᏓᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎾᎵᏝᎢᏙ ᏴᏫ ᏢᏅ ᏍᎫ Ꮲ ᏳᏩᏂᎷᎦ ᎤᎾ ᏭᏅᏏ ᏩᏂᎷᎦ
segments.transliteration: igohidadv gehv analitlaido yvwi tlvnv sgu tlv yuwaniluga una wunvsi waniluga
segments.translation: People are always on the run and they're not going anywhere.
